data.title: Use materials creatively
data.subject: Art and design
data.description: to use a range of materials creatively to design and make products

data.title: Drawing, painting and sculpture
data.subject: Art and design
data.description: to use drawing, painting and sculpture to develop and share their ideas, experiences and imagination

data.title: Techniques
data.subject: Art and design
data.description: to develop a wide range of art and design techniques in using colour, pattern, texture, line, shape, form and space

data.title: Artists, craft makers and designers
data.subject: Art and design
data.description: about the work of a range of artists, craft makers and designers, describing the differences and similarities between different practices and disciplines, and making links to their own work.

data.title: Sketch books
data.subject: Art and design
data.description: to create sketch books to record their observations and use them to review and revisit ideas

data.title: Mastery of techniques
data.subject: Art and design
data.description: to improve their mastery of art and design techniques, including drawing, painting and sculpture with a range of materials [for example, pencil, charcoal, paint, clay]

data.title: Great artists, architects and designers
data.subject: Art and design
data.description: about great artists, architects and designers in history.

data.title: Algorithms and programs
data.subject: Computing
data.description: understand what algorithms are; how they are implemented as programs on digital devices; and that programs execute by following precise and unambiguous instructions

data.title: Create and debug
data.subject: Computing
data.description: create and debug simple programs

data.title: Logical reasoning
data.subject: Computing
data.description: use logical reasoning to predict the behaviour of simple programs

data.title: Digital content
data.subject: Computing
data.description: use technology purposefully to create, organise, store, manipulate and retrieve digital content

data.title: IT beyond school
data.subject: Computing
data.description: recognise common uses of information technology beyond school

data.title: Safety and privacy
data.subject: Computing
data.description: use technology safely and respectfully, keeping personal information private; identify where to go for help and support when they have concerns about content or contact on the internet or other online technologies.

data.title: Design, write and debug programs
data.subject: Computing
data.description: design, write and debug programs that accomplish specific goals, including controlling or simulating physical systems; solve problems by decomposing them into smaller parts

data.title: Sequence, selection, and repetition
data.subject: Computing
data.description: use sequence, selection, and repetition in programs; work with variables and various forms of input and output

data.title: Logical reasoning and error detection
data.subject: Computing
data.description: use logical reasoning to explain how some simple algorithms work and to detect and correct errors in algorithms and programs

data.title: Computer networks
data.subject: Computing
data.description: understand computer networks including the internet; how they can provide multiple services, such as the world wide web; and the opportunities they offer for communication and collaboration

data.title: Search technologies
data.subject: Computing
data.description: use search technologies effectively, appreciate how results are selected and ranked, and be discerning in evaluating digital content

data.title: Select and combine software
data.subject: Computing
data.description: select, use and combine a variety of software (including internet services) on a range of digital devices to design and create a range of programs, systems and content that accomplish given goals, including collecting, analysing, evaluating and presenting data and information

data.title: Safety and responsibility
data.subject: Computing
data.description: use technology safely, respectfully and responsibly; recognise acceptable/unacceptable behaviour; identify a range of ways to report concerns about content and contact.

data.title: Healthy diet principles
data.subject: Design and technology
data.description: use the basic principles of a healthy and varied diet to prepare dishes

data.title: Source of food
data.subject: Design and technology
data.description: understand where food comes from.

data.title: Design purposeful products
data.subject: Design and technology
data.description: design purposeful, functional, appealing products for themselves and other users based on design criteria

data.title: Generate and communicate ideas
data.subject: Design and technology
data.description: generate, develop, model and communicate their ideas through talking, drawing, templates, mock-ups and, where appropriate, information and communication technology

data.title: Explore existing products
data.subject: Design and technology
data.description: explore and evaluate a range of existing products

data.title: Evaluate ideas and products
data.subject: Design and technology
data.description: evaluate their ideas and products against design criteria

data.title: Select and use tools
data.subject: Design and technology
data.description: select from and use a range of tools and equipment to perform practical tasks [for example, cutting, shaping, joining and finishing]

data.title: Select and use materials
data.subject: Design and technology
data.description: select from and use a wide range of materials and components, including construction materials, textiles and ingredients, according to their characteristics

data.title: Build structures
data.subject: Design and technology
data.description: build structures, exploring how they can be made stronger, stiffer and more stable

data.title: Explore mechanisms
data.subject: Design and technology
data.description: explore and use mechanisms [for example, levers, sliders, wheels and axles], in their products.

data.title: Apply healthy diet principles
data.subject: Design and technology
data.description: understand and apply the principles of a healthy and varied diet

data.title: Prepare and cook dishes
data.subject: Design and technology
data.description: prepare and cook a variety of predominantly savoury dishes using a range of cooking techniques

data.title: Seasonality and ingredients
data.subject: Design and technology
data.description: understand seasonality, and know where and how a variety of ingredients are grown, reared, caught and processed.

data.title: Use research and design criteria
data.subject: Design and technology
data.description: use research and develop design criteria to inform the design of innovative, functional, appealing products that are fit for purpose, aimed at particular individuals or groups

data.title: Generate and communicate ideas
data.subject: Design and technology
data.description: generate, develop, model and communicate their ideas through discussion, annotated sketches, cross-sectional and exploded diagrams, prototypes, pattern pieces and computer-aided design

data.title: Analyse existing products
data.subject: Design and technology
data.description: investigate and analyse a range of existing products

data.title: Evaluate against criteria
data.subject: Design and technology
data.description: evaluate their ideas and products against their own design criteria and consider the views of others to improve their work

data.title: Key events and individuals
data.subject: Design and technology
data.description: understand how key events and individuals in design and technology have helped shape the world

data.title: Select and use tools accurately
data.subject: Design and technology
data.description: select from and use a wider range of tools and equipment to perform practical tasks [for example, cutting, shaping, joining and finishing], accurately

data.title: Select and use materials
data.subject: Design and technology
data.description: select from and use a wider range of materials and components, including construction materials, textiles and ingredients, according to their functional properties and aesthetic qualities

data.title: Strengthen structures
data.subject: Design and technology
data.description: apply their understanding of how to strengthen, stiffen and reinforce more complex structures

data.title: Mechanical systems
data.subject: Design and technology
data.description: understand and use mechanical systems in their products [for example, gears, pulleys, cams, levers and linkages]

data.title: Electrical systems
data.subject: Design and technology
data.description: understand and use electrical systems in their products [for example, series circuits incorporating switches, bulbs, buzzers and motors]

data.title: Computing in products
data.subject: Design and technology
data.description: apply their understanding of computing to program, monitor and control their products.

data.notesAndGuidance: Pupils in years 1 and 2 should explore the world around them and raise their own questions. They should experience different types of scientific enquiries, including practical activities, and begin to recognise ways in which they might answer scientific questions.

data.title: Gathering and recording data
data.subject: Science
data.description: gathering and recording data to help in answering questions
data.notesAndGuidance: Pupils in years 1 and 2 should explore the world around them and raise their own questions. They should experience different types of scientific enquiries, including practical activities, and begin to recognise ways in which they might answer scientific questions.

data.title: Asking questions and using scientific enquiries
data.subject: Science
data.description: asking relevant questions and using different types of scientific enquiries to answer them
data.notesAndGuidance: Pupils in years 3 and 4 should be given a range of scientific experiences to enable them to raise their own questions about the world around them. They should start to make their own decisions about the most appropriate type of scientific enquiry they might use to answer questions; recognise when a simple fair test is necessary and help to decide how to set it up; talk about criteria for grouping, sorting and classifying; and use simple keys. They should begin to look for naturally occurring patterns and relationships and decide what data to collect to identify them.

data.title: Setting up practical enquiries and fair tests
data.subject: Science
data.description: setting up simple practical enquiries, comparative and fair tests
data.notesAndGuidance: Pupils should start to make their own decisions about the most appropriate type of scientific enquiry they might use to answer questions; recognise when a simple fair test is necessary and help to decide how to set it up.

data.title: Making observations and taking measurements
data.subject: Science
data.description: making systematic and careful observations and, where appropriate, taking accurate measurements using standard units, using a range of equipment, including thermometers and data loggers
data.notesAndGuidance: They should help to make decisions about what observations to make, how long to make them for and the type of simple equipment that might be used. They should learn how to use new equipment, such as data loggers, appropriately.

data.title: Gathering, recording, classifying and presenting data
data.subject: Science
data.description: gathering, recording, classifying and presenting data in a variety of ways to help in answering questions
data.notesAndGuidance: They should collect data from their own observations and measurements, using notes, simple tables and standard units, and help to make decisions about how to record and analyse this data.

data.title: Recording findings using scientific language and diagrams
data.subject: Science
data.description: recording findings using simple scientific language, drawings, labelled diagrams, keys, bar charts, and tables
data.notesAndGuidance: Pupils should use relevant scientific language to discuss their ideas and communicate their findings in ways that are appropriate for different audiences.

data.title: Reporting on findings from enquiries
data.subject: Science
data.description: reporting on findings from enquiries, including oral and written explanations, displays or presentations of results and conclusions
data.notesAndGuidance: Pupils should use relevant scientific language to discuss their ideas and communicate their findings in ways that are appropriate for different audiences.

data.title: Drawing conclusions and making predictions

data.notesAndGuidance: With help, pupils should look for changes, patterns, similarities and differences in their data in order to draw simple conclusions and answer questions. With support, they should identify new questions arising from the data, making predictions for new values within or beyond the data they have collected, and finding ways of improving what they have already done.

data.title: Identifying differences, similarities or changes

data.notesAndGuidance: With help, pupils should look for changes, patterns, similarities and differences in their data in order to draw simple conclusions and answer questions.

data.notesAndGuidance: They should also recognise when and how secondary sources might help them to answer questions that cannot be answered through practical investigations.

data.notesAndGuidance: Pupils in years 5 and 6 should use their science experiences to: explore ideas and raise different kinds of questions; select and plan the most appropriate type of scientific enquiry to use to answer scientific questions; recognise when and how to set up comparative and fair tests and explain which variables need to be controlled and why.

data.notesAndGuidance: They should decide how to record data from a choice of familiar approaches; look for different causal relationships in their data and identify evidence that refutes or supports their ideas.

data.title: Using test results to make predictions

data.notesAndGuidance: They should use their results to identify when further tests and observations might be needed; recognise which secondary sources will be most useful to research their ideas and begin to separate opinion from fact.

data.notesAndGuidance: They should use relevant scientific language and illustrations to discuss, communicate and justify their scientific ideas and should talk about how scientific ideas have developed over time.

data.notesAndGuidance: They should look for different causal relationships in their data and identify evidence that refutes or supports their ideas. They should recognise which secondary sources will be most useful to research their ideas and begin to separate opinion from fact.

data.title: Identify and name common animals
data.subject: Science
data.description: identify and name a variety of common animals including fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals
data.notesAndGuidance: Pupils should use the local environment throughout the year to explore and answer questions about animals in their habitat. They should understand how to take care of animals taken from their local environment and the need to return them safely after study. Pupils should become familiar with the common names of some fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals, including those that are kept as pets. Pupils should have plenty of opportunities to learn the names of the main body parts (including head, neck, arms, elbows, legs, knees, face, ears, eyes, hair, mouth, teeth) through games, actions, songs and rhymes.
data.workingScientifically: Pupils might work scientifically by: using their observations to compare and contrast animals at first hand or through videos and photographs, describing how they identify and group them; grouping animals according to what they eat; and using their senses to compare different textures, sounds and smells.

data.subject: Science
data.description: identify and name a variety of common wild and garden plants, including deciduous and evergreen trees
data.notesAndGuidance: Pupils should use the local environment throughout the year to explore and answer questions about plants growing in their habitat. Where possible, they should observe the growth of flowers and vegetables that they have planted. They should become familiar with common names of flowers, examples of deciduous and evergreen trees, and plant structures (including leaves, flowers (blossom), petals, fruit, roots, bulb, seed, trunk, branches, stem).
data.workingScientifically: Pupils might work scientifically by: observing closely, perhaps using magnifying glasses, and comparing and contrasting familiar plants; describing how they were able to identify and group them, and drawing diagrams showing the parts of different plants including trees. Pupils might keep records of how plants have changed over time, for example, the leaves falling off trees and buds opening; and compare and contrast what they have found out about different plants.

data.workingScientifically: Pupils might work scientifically by: observing closely, perhaps using magnifying glasses, and comparing and contrasting familiar plants; describing how they were able to identify and group them, and drawing diagrams showing the parts of different plants including trees. Pupils might keep records of how plants have changed over time, for example, the leaves falling off trees and buds opening; and compare and contrast what they have found out about different plants.

data.notesAndGuidance: Pupils should be introduced to the basic needs of animals for survival, as well as the importance of exercise and nutrition for humans. data.title: Living, dead, and never alive
data.subject: Science
data.description: explore and compare the differences between things that are living, dead, and things that have never been alive
data.notesAndGuidance: Pupils should be introduced to the idea that all living things have certain characteristics that are essential for keeping them alive and healthy. They should raise and answer questions that help them to become familiar with the life processes that are common to all living things. Pupils should be introduced to the terms 'habitat' and 'microhabitat'. They should raise and answer questions about the local environment that help them to identify and study a variety of plants and animals within their habitat and observe how living things depend on each other. Pupils should compare animals in familiar habitats with animals found in less familiar habitats, for example, on the seashore, in woodland, in the ocean, in the rainforest.
data.workingScientifically: Pupils might work scientifically by: sorting and classifying things according to whether they are living, dead or were never alive, and recording their findings using charts. They could construct a simple food chain that includes humans (eg, grass, cow, human). They could describe the conditions in different habitats and microhabitats and find out how the conditions affect the number and types of plants and animals that live there.

data.title: Seeds and bulbs growing

data.title: Plant needs for growth

data.workingScientifically: Pupils might work scientifically by: observing and recording, with some accuracy, the growth of a variety of plants as they change over time from a seed or bulb; setting up a comparative test to show that plants need light and water to stay healthy.

data.title: Suitability of everyday materials
data.subject: Science
data.description: identify and compare the suitability of a variety of everyday materials, including wood, metal, plastic, glass, brick, rock, paper and cardboard for particular uses
data.notesAndGuidance: Pupils should identify and discuss the uses of different everyday materials so that they become familiar with how some materials are used for more than one thing or different materials are used for the same thing. They should think about the properties of materials that make them suitable or unsuitable for particular purposes and they should be encouraged to think about unusual and creative uses for everyday materials. Pupils might find out about people who have developed useful new materials, for example John Dunlop, Charles Macintosh or John McAdam.
data.workingScientifically: Pupils might work scientifically by: comparing the uses of everyday materials in and around the school with materials found in other places; observing closely, identifying and classifying the uses of different materials, and recording their observations.

data.title: Changing shapes of solid objects

data.notesAndGuidance: Pupils should identify and discuss the uses of different everyday materials so that they become familiar with how some materials are used for more than one thing or different materials are used for the same thing.
data.workingScientifically: Pupils might work scientifically by: comparing the uses of everyday materials in and around the school with materials found in other places; observing closely, identifying and classifying the uses of different materials, and recording their observations.

data.title: Animal and human nutrition
data.subject: Science

data.notesAndGuidance: Pupils should continue to learn about the importance of nutrition and should be introduced to the main body parts associated with the skeleton and muscles, finding out how different parts of the body have special functions.

data.title: Skeletons and muscles

data.workingScientifically: Pupils might work scientifically by: identifying and grouping animals with and without skeletons and observing and comparing their movement; exploring ideas about what would happen if humans did not have skeletons.

data.title: Movement on different surfaces
data.subject: Science
data.description: compare how things move on different surfaces
data.notesAndGuidance: Pupils should observe that magnetic forces can act without direct contact, unlike most forces, where direct contact is necessary (for example, opening a door, pushing a swing).
data.workingScientifically: Pupils might work scientifically by: comparing how different things move and grouping them; raising questions and carrying out tests to find out how far things move on different surfaces, and gathering and recording data to find answers to their questions.

data.title: Contact and non-contact forces
data.subject: Science
data.description: notice that some forces need contact between 2 objects, but magnetic forces can act at a distance
data.notesAndGuidance: Pupils should observe that magnetic forces can act without direct contact, unlike most forces, where direct contact is necessary (for example, opening a door, pushing a swing).
data.workingScientifically: Pupils might work scientifically by: comparing how different things move and grouping them.

data.title: Magnetic attraction and repulsion
data.subject: Science
data.description: observe how magnets attract or repel each other and attract some materials and not others

data.title: Grouping magnetic materials
data.subject: Science
data.description: compare and group together a variety of everyday materials on the basis of whether they are attracted to a magnet, and identify some magnetic materials
data.notesAndGuidance: They should explore the behaviour and everyday uses of different magnets (for example, bar, ring, button and horseshoe).

data.title: Magnetic poles

data.title: Grouping living things

data.workingScientifically: Pupils might work scientifically by: using and making simple guides or keys to explore and identify local plants and animals; making a guide to local living things.

data.title: Using classification keys
data.subject: Science

data.title: Environmental changes and dangers

data.workingScientifically: Pupils might work scientifically by: raising and answering questions based on their observations of animals and what they have found out about other animals that they have researched.

data.title: Grouping solids, liquids and gases

data.title: Evaporation, condensation and the water cycle

data.title: How sounds are made (vibrations)

data.title: Patterns between pitch and object features

data.title: Sound fading over distance

data.notesAndGuidance: Pupils should explore and identify the way sound is made through vibration in a range of different musical instruments from around the world.

data.title: Human development to old age

data.title: Earth's rotation, day and night

data.description: explain that unsupported objects fall towards the Earth because of the force of gravity acting between the Earth and the falling object
data.notesAndGuidance: Pupils should explore falling objects and raise questions about the effects of air resistance. They should explore the effects of air resistance by observing how different objects such as parachutes and sycamore seeds fall.
data.workingScientifically: Pupils might work scientifically by: exploring falling paper cones or cupcake cases, and designing and making a variety of parachutes and carrying out fair tests to determine which designs are the most effective.

data.title: Air resistance, water resistance and friction
data.subject: Science
data.description: identify the effects of air resistance, water resistance and friction, that act between moving surfaces
data.notesAndGuidance: Pupils should experience forces that make things begin to move, get faster or slow down. Pupils should explore the effects of friction on movement and find out how it slows or stops moving objects.
data.workingScientifically: They might explore resistance in water by making and testing boats of different shapes.

data.title: Mechanisms and force effects
data.subject: Science
data.description: recognise that some mechanisms including levers, pulleys and gears allow a smaller force to have a greater effect
data.notesAndGuidance: Pupils should explore the effects of levers, pulleys and simple machines on movement.
data.workingScientifically: They might design and make products that use levers, pulleys, gears and/or springs and explore their effects.

data.title: Differences in life cycles
data.subject: Science
data.description: describe the differences in the life cycles of a mammal, an amphibian, an insect and a bird
data.notesAndGuidance: Pupils should study and raise questions about their local environment throughout the year. They should observe life-cycle changes in a variety of living things, for example, plants in the vegetable garden or flower border, and animals in the local environment. They should find out about the work of naturalists and animal behaviourists, for example, David Attenborough and Jane Goodall.
data.workingScientifically: Pupils might work scientifically by: observing and comparing the life cycles of plants and animals in their local environment with other plants and animals around the world; asking pertinent questions and suggesting reasons for similarities and differences.

data.title: Reproduction in plants and animals
data.subject: Science
data.description: describe the life process of reproduction in some plants and animals
data.notesAndGuidance: Pupils should find out about different types of reproduction, including sexual and asexual reproduction in plants, and sexual reproduction in animals.
data.workingScientifically: They might try to grow new plants from different parts of the parent plant, for example, seeds, stem and root cuttings, tubers, bulbs. They might observe changes in an animal over a period of time, comparing how different animals reproduce and grow.

data.title: Compare and group everyday materials
data.subject: Science
data.description: compare and group together everyday materials on the basis of their properties, including their hardness, solubility, transparency, conductivity (electrical and thermal), and response to magnets
data.notesAndGuidance: Pupils should build a more systematic understanding of materials by exploring and comparing the properties of a broad range of materials, including relating these to what they learnt about magnetism in year 3 and about electricity in year 4.
data.workingScientifically: Pupils might work scientifically by: carrying out tests to answer questions, for example, 'Which materials would be the most effective for making a warm jacket, for wrapping ice cream to stop it melting, or for making blackout curtains?'

data.title: Dissolving and recovering substances
data.subject: Science
data.description: know that some materials will dissolve in liquid to form a solution, and describe how to recover a substance from a solution
data.notesAndGuidance: They should explore reversible changes, including evaporating, filtering, sieving, melting and dissolving, recognising that melting and dissolving are different processes.
data.workingScientifically: They might compare materials in order to make a switch in a circuit.

data.title: Separating mixtures
data.subject: Science
data.description: use knowledge of solids, liquids and gases to decide how mixtures might be separated, including through filtering, sieving and evaporating
data.notesAndGuidance: They should explore reversible changes, including evaporating, filtering, sieving, melting and dissolving, recognising that melting and dissolving are different processes.
data.workingScientifically: Pupils might work scientifically by: carrying out tests to answer questions.

data.title: Reasons for uses of everyday materials
data.subject: Science
data.description: give reasons, based on evidence from comparative and fair tests, for the particular uses of everyday materials, including metals, wood and plastic
data.notesAndGuidance: Pupils should build a more systematic understanding of materials by exploring and comparing the properties of a broad range of materials.
data.workingScientifically: Pupils might work scientifically by: carrying out tests to answer questions, for example, 'Which materials would be the most effective for making a warm jacket, for wrapping ice cream to stop it melting, or for making blackout curtains?'

data.title: Reversible changes
data.subject: Science
data.description: demonstrate that dissolving, mixing and changes of state are reversible changes
data.notesAndGuidance: They should explore reversible changes, including evaporating, filtering, sieving, melting and dissolving, recognising that melting and dissolving are different processes.
data.workingScientifically: They could observe and compare the changes that take place when burning different materials or baking bread or cakes.

data.title: Irreversible changes and new materials
data.subject: Science
data.description: explain that some changes result in the formation of new materials, and that this kind of change is not usually reversible, including changes associated with burning and the action of acid on bicarbonate of soda
data.notesAndGuidance: Pupils should explore changes that are difficult to reverse, for example, burning, rusting and other reactions, for example, vinegar with bicarbonate of soda.
data.workingScientifically: They could observe and compare the changes that take place when burning different materials or baking bread or cakes. They might research and discuss how chemical changes have an impact on our lives.

data.title: Human circulatory system
data.subject: Science
data.description: identify and name the main parts of the human circulatory system, and describe the functions of the heart, blood vessels and blood
data.notesAndGuidance: Pupils should build on their learning from years 3 and 4 about the main body parts and internal organs to explore and answer questions that help them to understand how the circulatory system enables the body to function.
data.workingScientifically: Pupils might work scientifically by: exploring the work of scientists and scientific research about the relationship between diet, exercise, drugs, lifestyle and health.

data.title: Impact of diet, exercise, drugs and lifestyle
data.subject: Science
data.description: recognise the impact of diet, exercise, drugs and lifestyle on the way their bodies function
data.notesAndGuidance: Pupils should learn how to keep their bodies healthy and how their bodies might be damaged - including how some drugs and other substances can be harmful to the human body.
data.workingScientifically: Pupils might work scientifically by: exploring the work of scientists and scientific research about the relationship between diet, exercise, drugs, lifestyle and health.

data.title: Transport of nutrients and water
data.subject: Science
data.description: describe the ways in which nutrients and water are transported within animals, including humans
data.notesAndGuidance: Pupils should build on their learning from years 3 and 4 about the main body parts and internal organs to explore and answer questions that help them to understand how the circulatory system enables the body to function.
data.workingScientifically: Pupils might work scientifically by: exploring the work of scientists and scientific research about the relationship between diet, exercise, drugs, lifestyle and health.

data.title: Brightness of a lamp or volume of a buzzer
data.subject: Science
data.description: associate the brightness of a lamp or the volume of a buzzer with the number and voltage of cells used in the circuit
data.notesAndGuidance: Building on their work in year 4, pupils should construct simple series circuits, to help them to answer questions about what happens when they try different components, for example, switches, bulbs, buzzers and motors.
data.workingScientifically: Pupils might work scientifically by: systematically identifying the effect of changing one component at a time in a circuit.

data.title: Variations in how components function
data.subject: Science
data.description: compare and give reasons for variations in how components function, including the brightness of bulbs, the loudness of buzzers and the on/off position of switches
data.notesAndGuidance: Building on their work in year 4, pupils should construct simple series circuits, to help them to answer questions about what happens when they try different components.
data.workingScientifically: Pupils might work scientifically by: systematically identifying the effect of changing one component at a time in a circuit; designing and making a set of traffic lights, a burglar alarm or some other useful circuit.

data.title: Recognised symbols for simple circuits
data.subject: Science
data.description: use recognised symbols when representing a simple circuit in a diagram
data.notesAndGuidance: They should learn how to represent a simple circuit in a diagram using recognised symbols. Note: pupils are expected to learn only about series circuits, not parallel circuits.
data.workingScientifically: Pupils might work scientifically by: designing and making a set of traffic lights, a burglar alarm or some other useful circuit.

data.title: Living things change over time and fossils
data.subject: Science
data.description: recognise that living things have changed over time and that fossils provide information about living things that inhabited the Earth millions of years ago
data.notesAndGuidance: Building on what they learned about fossils in the topic on rocks in year 3, pupils should find out more about how living things on earth have changed over time.
data.workingScientifically: Pupils might work scientifically by: observing and raising questions about local animals and how they are adapted to their environment; comparing how some living things are adapted to survive in extreme conditions.

data.title: Offspring vary and are not identical to parents
data.subject: Science
data.description: recognise that living things produce offspring of the same kind, but normally offspring vary and are not identical to their parents
data.notesAndGuidance: They should be introduced to the idea that characteristics are passed from parents to their offspring, for instance by considering different breeds of dogs.
data.workingScientifically: Pupils might work scientifically by: observing and raising questions about local animals and how they are adapted to their environment.

data.title: Adaptation and evolution
data.subject: Science
data.description: identify how animals and plants are adapted to suit their environment in different ways and that adaptation may lead to evolution
data.notesAndGuidance: They should also appreciate that variation in offspring over time can make animals more or less able to survive in particular environments.
data.workingScientifically: They might analyse the advantages and disadvantages of specific adaptations, such as being on 2 feet rather than 4, having a long or a short beak, having gills or lungs.

data.title: Light travels in straight lines
data.subject: Science
data.description: recognise that light appears to travel in straight lines
data.notesAndGuidance: Pupils should build on the work on light in year 3, exploring the way that light behaves, including light sources, reflection and shadows. They should talk about what happens and make predictions.
data.workingScientifically: Pupils might work scientifically by: deciding where to place rear-view mirrors on cars; designing and making a periscope and using the idea that light appears to travel in straight lines to explain how it works.

data.title: Objects are seen because they give out or reflect light
data.subject: Science
data.description: use the idea that light travels in straight lines to explain that objects are seen because they give out or reflect light into the eye
data.notesAndGuidance: Pupils should build on the work on light in year 3, exploring the way that light behaves, including light sources, reflection and shadows.
data.workingScientifically: They might investigate the relationship between light sources, objects and shadows by using shadow puppets.

data.title: How we see things
data.subject: Science
data.description: explain that we see things because light travels from light sources to our eyes or from light sources to objects and then to our eyes
data.notesAndGuidance: Pupils should build on the work on light in year 3, exploring the way that light behaves, including light sources, reflection and shadows.
data.workingScientifically: They might investigate the relationship between light sources, objects and shadows by using shadow puppets.

data.title: Shadows have the same shape as objects
data.subject: Science
data.description: use the idea that light travels in straight lines to explain why shadows have the same shape as the objects that cast them
data.notesAndGuidance: Pupils should build on the work on light in year 3, exploring the way that light behaves, including light sources, reflection and shadows.
data.workingScientifically: They might investigate the relationship between light sources, objects and shadows by using shadow puppets.

data.title: Classify living things into broad groups
data.subject: Science
data.description: describe how living things are classified into broad groups according to common observable characteristics and based on similarities and differences, including micro-organisms, plants and animals
data.notesAndGuidance: Pupils should build on their learning about grouping living things in year 4 by looking at the classification system in more detail. They should be introduced to the idea that broad groupings, such as micro-organisms, plants and animals can be subdivided. Through direct observations where possible, they should classify animals into commonly found invertebrates (such as insects, spiders, snails, worms) and vertebrates (fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals).
data.workingScientifically: Pupils might work scientifically by: using classification systems and keys to identify some animals and plants in the immediate environment. They could research unfamiliar animals and plants from a broad range of other habitats and decide where they belong in the classification system.

data.title: Give reasons for classifying plants and animals
data.subject: Science
data.description: give reasons for classifying plants and animals based on specific characteristics
data.notesAndGuidance: They should discuss reasons why living things are placed in one group and not another.
data.workingScientifically: Pupils might work scientifically by: using classification systems and keys to identify some animals and plants in the immediate environment.

data.title: SL.11-12.1
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Initiate and participate effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grades 11–12 topics, texts, and issues, building on others’ ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

data.title: SL.11-12.1a
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read and researched material under study; explicitly draw on that preparation by referring to evidence from texts and other research on the topic or issue to stimulate a thoughtful, well-reasoned exchange of ideas.

data.title: SL.11-12.1b
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Work with peers to promote civil, democratic discussions and decision-making, set clear goals and deadlines, and establish individual roles as needed.

data.title: SL.11-12.1c
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Propel conversations by posing and responding to questions that probe reasoning and evidence; ensure a hearing for a full range of positions on a topic or issue; clarify, verify, or challenge ideas and conclusions; and promote divergent and creative perspectives.

data.title: SL.11-12.1d
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Respond thoughtfully to diverse perspectives; synthesize comments, claims, and evidence made on all sides of an issue; resolve contradictions when possible; and determine what additional information or research is required to deepen the investigation or complete the task.

data.title: SL.11-12.2
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Integrate multiple sources of information presented in diverse formats and media (e.g., visually, quantitatively, orally) in order to make informed decisions and solve problems, evaluating the credibility and accuracy of each source and noting any discrepancies among the data.

data.title: SL.11-12.3
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Evaluate a speaker’s point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric, assessing the stance, premises, links among ideas, word choice, points of emphasis, and tone used.

data.title: SL.11-12.4
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence, conveying a clear and distinct perspective, such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning, alternative or opposing perspectives are addressed, and the organization, development, substance, and style are appropriate to purpose, audience, and a range of formal and informal tasks.

data.title: SL.11-12.5
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Make strategic use of digital media (e.g., textual, graphical, audio, visual, and interactive elements) in presentations to enhance understanding of findings, reasoning, and evidence and to add interest.

data.title: SL.11-12.6
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, demonstrating a command of formal English when indicated or appropriate. (See grades 11–12 Language standards 1 and 3 on page 54 for specific expectations.)

data.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

data.title: L.6.1a
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Ensure that pronouns are in the proper case (subjective, objective, possessive).

data.title: L.6.1b
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Use intensive pronouns (e.g., myself, ourselves).

data.title: L.6.1c
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Recognize and correct inappropriate shifts in pronoun number and person.

data.title: L.6.1d
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Recognize and correct vague pronouns (i.e., ones with unclear or ambiguous antecedents).

data.title: L.6.1e
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Recognize variations from standard English in their own and others’ writing and speaking, and identify and use strategies to improve expression in conventional language.

data.title: L.6.2
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

data.title: L.6.2a
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Use punctuation (commas, parentheses, dashes) to set off nonrestrictive/parenthetical elements.

data.title: L.6.2b
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Spell correctly.

data.title: L.6.3
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

data.title: L.6.3a
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Vary sentence patterns for meaning, reader/listener interest, and style.

data.title: L.6.3b
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Maintain consistency in style and tone.

data.title: L.6.4
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 6 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

data.title: L.6.4a
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Use context (e.g., the overall meaning of a sentence or paragraph; a word’s position or function in a sentence) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

data.title: L.6.4b
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek or Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word (e.g., audience, auditory, audible).

data.title: L.6.4c
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Consult reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation of a word or determine or clarify its precise meaning or its part of speech.

data.title: L.6.4d
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Verify the preliminary determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (e.g., by checking the inferred meaning in context or in a dictionary).

data.title: L.6.5
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

data.title: L.6.5a
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Interpret figures of speech (e.g., personification) in context.

data.title: L.6.5b
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Use the relationship between particular words (e.g., cause/effect, part/whole, item/category) to better understand each of the words.

data.title: L.6.5c
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Distinguish among the connotations (associations) of words with similar denotations (definitions) (e.g., stingy, scrimping, economical, unwasteful, thrifty).

data.title: L.6.6
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases; gather vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

data.description: Use various types of phrases (noun, verb, adjectival, adverbial, participial, prepositional, absolute) and clauses (independent, dependent; noun, relative, adverbial) to convey specific meanings and add variety and interest to writing or presentations.

data.subject: English Language Arts

data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Write and edit work so that it conforms to the guidelines in a style manual (e.g., MLA Handbook, Turabian’s Manual for Writers) appropriate for the discipline and writing type.

data.title: L.9-10.4b
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Identify and correctly use patterns of word changes that indicate different meanings or parts of speech (e.g., analyze, analysis, analytical; advocate, advocacy).

data.title: L.9-10.4c
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Consult general and specialized reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation of a word or determine or clarify its precise meaning, its part of speech, or its etymology.

data.subject: English Language Arts

data.title: L.K.4b
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Use the most frequently occurring inflections and affixes (e.g., -ed, -s, re-, un-, pre-, -ful, -less) as a clue to the meaning of an unknown word.

data.title: L.K.5
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: With guidance and support from adults, explore word relationships and nuances in word meanings.

data.title: L.K.5a

data.description: Sort common objects into categories (e.g., shapes, foods) to gain a sense of the concepts the categories represent.

data.title: L.K.5b
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Demonstrate understanding of frequently occurring verbs and adjectives by relating them to their opposites (antonyms).

data.title: L.K.5c
data.subject: English Language Arts

data.title: L.K.5d
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Distinguish shades of meaning among verbs describing the same general action (e.g., walk, march, strut, prance) by acting out the meanings.

data.title: W.11-12.1
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

data.title: W.11-12.10
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

data.title: W.11-12.1.a
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Introduce precise, knowledgeable claim(s), establish the significance of the claim(s), distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims, and create an organization that logically sequences claim(s), counterclaims, reasons, and evidence.

data.title: W.11-12.1.b
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Develop claim(s) and counterclaims fairly and thoroughly, supplying the most relevant evidence for each while pointing out the strengths and limitations of both in a manner that anticipates the audience’s knowledge level, concerns, values, and possible biases.

data.title: W.11-12.1.c
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Use words, phrases, and clauses as well as varied syntax to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships between claim(s) and reasons, between reasons and evidence, and between claim(s) and counterclaims.

data.title: W.11-12.1.d
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.

data.title: W.11-12.1.e
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the argument presented.

data.title: W.11-12.2
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas, concepts, and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

data.title: W.11-12.2.a
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Introduce a topic; organize complex ideas, concepts, and information so that each new element builds on that which precedes it to create a unified whole; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., figures, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

data.title: W.11-12.2.b
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Develop the topic thoroughly by selecting the most significant and relevant facts, extended definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples appropriate to the audience’s knowledge of the topic.

data.title: W.11-12.2.c
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Use appropriate and varied transitions and syntax to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships among complex ideas and concepts.

data.title: W.11-12.2.d
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Use precise language, domain-specific vocabulary, and techniques such as metaphor, simile, and analogy to manage the complexity of the topic.

data.title: W.11-12.2.e
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.

data.title: W.11-12.2.f
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented (e.g., articulating implications or the significance of the topic).

data.title: W.11-12.3
data.subject: English Language Arts

data.title: W.11-12.3.a

data.title: W.11-12.3.b
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, pacing, description, reflection, and multiple plot lines, to develop experiences, events, and/or characters.

data.title: W.11-12.3.c
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Use a variety of techniques to sequence events so that they build on one another to create a coherent whole and build toward a particular tone and outcome (e.g., a sense of mystery, suspense, growth, or resolution).

data.title: W.11-12.3.d
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Use precise words and phrases, telling details, and sensory language to convey a vivid picture of the experiences, events, setting, and/or characters.

data.title: W.11-12.3.e
data.subject: English Language Arts
data.description: Provide a conclusion that follows from and reflects on what is experienced, observed, or resolved over the course of the narrative.

data.title: W.11-12.4

data.title: Distinguish defining attributes of shapes
data.cluster: Reason with shapes and their attributes.
data.description: Distinguish between defining attributes (e.g., triangles are closed and three-sided) versus non-defining attributes (e.g., color, orientation, overall size); build and draw shapes to possess defining attributes.

data.title: Compose two-dimensional and three-dimensional shapes
data.cluster: Reason with shapes and their attributes.
data.description: Compose two-dimensional shapes (rectangles, squares, trapezoids, triangles, half-circles, and quarter-circles) or three-dimensional shapes (cubes, right rectangular prisms, right circular cones, and right circular cylinders) to create a composite shape, and compose new shapes from the composite shape.

data.title: Partition circles and rectangles
data.cluster: Reason with shapes and their attributes.
data.description: Partition circles and rectangles into two and four equal shares, describe the shares using the words halves, fourths, and quarters, and use the phrases half of, fourth of, and quarter of. Describe the whole as two of, or four of the shares. Understand for these examples that decomposing into more equal shares creates smaller shares.

data.title: Order and compare objects by length
data.cluster: Measure lengths indirectly and by iterating length units.
data.description: Order three objects by length; compare the lengths of two objects indirectly by using a third object.

data.title: Measure length with length units
data.cluster: Measure lengths indirectly and by iterating length units.
data.description: Express the length of an object as a whole number of length units, by laying multiple copies of a shorter object (the length unit) end to end; understand that the length measurement of an object is the number of same-size length units that span it with no gaps or overlaps. Limit to contexts where the object being measured is spanned by a whole number of length units with no gaps or overlaps.

data.title: Tell and write time
data.description: Tell and write time in hours and half-hours using analog and digital clocks.

data.title: Represent and interpret data
data.description: Organize, represent, and interpret data with up to three categories; ask and answer questions about the total number of data points, how many in each category, and how many more or less are in one category than in another.

data.title: Count to 120
data.description: Count to 120, starting at any number less than 120. In this range, read and write numerals and represent a number of objects with a written numeral.

data.title: Understand place value of two-digit numbers
data.description: Understand that the two digits of a two-digit number represent amounts of tens and ones. Understand the following as special cases:

data.title: 10 as a bundle of ten ones
data.description: 10 can be thought of as a bundle of ten ones — called a “ten.”

data.title: Composition of numbers 11 to 19
data.description: The numbers from 11 to 19 are composed of a ten and one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine ones.

data.title: Multiples of 10
data.description: The numbers 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90 refer to one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine tens (and 0 ones).

data.title: Compare two-digit numbers
data.description: Compare two two-digit numbers based on meanings of the tens and ones digits, recording the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, and <.

data.title: Add within 100
data.cluster: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to add and subtract.
data.description: Add within 100, including adding a two-digit number and a one-digit number, and adding a two-digit number and a multiple of 10, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used. Understand that in adding two-digit numbers, one adds tens and tens, ones and ones; and sometimes it is necessary to compose a ten.

data.title: Mentally find 10 more or 10 less
data.cluster: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to add and subtract.
data.description: Given a two-digit number, mentally find 10 more or 10 less than the number, without having to count; explain the reasoning used.

data.title: Subtract multiples of 10
data.cluster: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to add and subtract.
data.description: Subtract multiples of 10 in the range 10-90 from multiples of 10 in the range 10-90 (positive or zero differences), using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used.

data.title: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction
data.cluster: Represent and solve problems involving addition and subtraction.
data.description: Use addition and subtraction within 20 to solve word problems involving situations of adding to, taking from, putting together, taking apart, and comparing, with unknowns in all positions, e.g., by using objects, drawings, and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

data.title: Solve word problems with three whole numbers
data.cluster: Represent and solve problems involving addition and subtraction.
data.description: Solve word problems that call for addition of three whole numbers whose sum is less than or equal to 20, e.g., by using objects, drawings, and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

data.title: Apply properties of operations
data.cluster: Understand and apply properties of operations and the relationship between addition and subtraction.
data.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add and subtract. Examples: If 8 + 3 = 11 is known, then 3 + 8 = 11 is also known. (Commutative property of addition.) To add 2 + 6 + 4, the second two numbers can be added to make a ten, so 2 + 6 + 4 = 2 + 10 = 12. (Associative property of addition.)

data.title: Subtraction as unknown-addend problem
data.cluster: Understand and apply properties of operations and the relationship between addition and subtraction.
data.description: Understand subtraction as an unknown-addend problem. For example, subtract 10 – 8 by finding the number that makes 10 when added to 8.

data.title: Relate counting to addition and subtraction
data.description: Relate counting to addition and subtraction (e.g., by counting on 2 to add 2).

data.title: Add and subtract within 20
data.description: Add and subtract within 20, demonstrating fluency for addition and subtraction within 10. Use strategies such as counting on; making ten (e.g., 8 + 6 = 8 + 2 + 4 = 10 + 4 = 14); decomposing a number leading to a ten (e.g., 13 – 4 = 13 – 3 – 1 = 10 – 1 = 9); using the relationship between addition and subtraction (e.g., knowing that 8 + 4 = 12, one knows 12 – 8 = 4); and creating equivalent but easier or known sums (e.g., adding 6 + 7 by creating the known equivalent 6 + 6 + 1 = 12 + 1 = 13).

data.title: Meaning of the equal sign
data.cluster: Work with addition and subtraction equations.
data.description: Understand the meaning of the equal sign, and determine if equations involving addition and subtraction are true or false. For example, which of the following equations are true and which are false? 6 = 6, 7 = 8 – 1, 5 + 2 = 2 + 5, 4 + 1 = 5 + 2.

data.title: Determine unknown whole number
data.cluster: Work with addition and subtraction equations.
data.description: Determine the unknown whole number in an addition or subtraction equation relating three whole numbers. For example, determine the unknown number that makes the equation true in each of the equations 8 + ? = 11, 5 = [] – 3, 6 + 6 = [].

data.title: Recognize and draw shapes
data.cluster: Reason with shapes and their attributes.
data.description: Recognize and draw shapes having specified attributes, such as a given number of angles or a given number of equal faces. Identify triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons, hexagons, and cubes.

data.title: Partition a rectangle
data.cluster: Reason with shapes and their attributes.
data.description: Partition a rectangle into rows and columns of same-size squares and count to find the total number of them.

data.title: Partition circles and rectangles into shares
data.cluster: Reason with shapes and their attributes.
data.description: Partition circles and rectangles into two, three, or four equal shares, describe the shares using the words halves, thirds, half of, a third of, etc., and describe the whole as two halves, three thirds, four fourths. Recognize that equal shares of identical wholes need not have the same shape.

data.title: Measure length with appropriate tools
data.cluster: Measure and estimate lengths in standard units.
data.description: Measure the length of an object by selecting and using appropriate tools such as rulers, yardsticks, meter sticks, and measuring tapes.

data.title: Draw picture and bar graphs
data.description: Draw a picture graph and a bar graph (with single-unit scale) to represent a data set with up to four categories. Solve simple put-together, take-apart, and compare problems using information presented in a bar graph.

data.title: Measure length with different units
data.cluster: Measure and estimate lengths in standard units.
data.description: Measure the length of an object twice, using length units of different lengths for the two measurements; describe how the two measurements relate to the size of the unit chosen.

data.title: Estimate lengths
data.cluster: Measure and estimate lengths in standard units.
data.description: Estimate lengths using units of inches, feet, centimeters, and meters.

data.title: Compare lengths of objects
data.cluster: Measure and estimate lengths in standard units.
data.description: Measure to determine how much longer one object is than another, expressing the length difference in terms of a standard length unit.

data.title: Solve word problems involving length
data.cluster: Relate addition and subtraction to length.
data.description: Use addition and subtraction within 100 to solve word problems involving lengths that are given in the same units, e.g., by using drawings (such as drawings of rulers) and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

data.title: Represent lengths on a number line
data.cluster: Relate addition and subtraction to length.
data.description: Represent whole numbers as lengths from 0 on a number line diagram with equally spaced points corresponding to the numbers 0, 1, 2, ..., and represent whole-number sums and differences within 100 on a number line diagram.

data.title: Tell and write time
data.description: Tell and write time from analog and digital clocks to the nearest five minutes, using a.m. and p.m.

data.title: Solve word problems with money
data.description: Solve word problems involving dollar bills, quarters, dimes, nickels, and pennies, using $ and ¢ symbols appropriately. Example: If you have 2 dimes and 3 pennies, how many cents do you have?

data.title: Generate measurement data and line plots
data.description: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths of several objects to the nearest whole unit, or by making repeated measurements of the same object. Show the measurements by making a line plot, where the horizontal scale is marked off in whole-number units.

data.title: Understand three-digit place value
data.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
data.description: Understand that the three digits of a three-digit number represent amounts of hundreds, tens, and ones; e.g., 706 equals 7 hundreds, 0 tens, and 6 ones. Understand the following as special cases:

data.title: 100 as a bundle of ten tens
data.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
data.description: 100 can be thought of as a bundle of ten tens — called a “hundred.”

data.title: Multiples of 100
data.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
data.description: The numbers 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 900 refer to one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine hundreds (and 0 tens and 0 ones).

data.title: Count within 1000
data.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
data.description: Count within 1000; skip-count by 5s, 10s, and 100s.

data.title: Read and write numbers to 1000
data.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
data.description: Read and write numbers to 1000 using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form.

data.title: Compare three-digit numbers
data.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
data.description: Compare two three-digit numbers based on meanings of the hundreds, tens, and ones digits, using >, =, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.

data.title: Fluently add and subtract within 100
data.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
data.cluster: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to add and subtract.
data.description: Fluently add and subtract within 100 using strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.

data.title: Add up to four two-digit numbers
data.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
data.cluster: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to add and subtract.
data.description: Add up to four two-digit numbers using strategies based on place value and properties of operations.

data.title: Add and subtract within 1000
data.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
data.cluster: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to add and subtract.
data.description: Add and subtract within 1000, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method. Understand that in adding or subtracting three-digit numbers, one adds or subtracts hundreds and hundreds, tens and tens, ones and ones; and sometimes it is necessary to compose or decompose tens or hundreds.

data.title: Mentally add or subtract 10 or 100
data.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
data.cluster: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to add and subtract.
data.description: Mentally add 10 or 100 to a given number 100–900, and mentally subtract 10 or 100 from a given number 100–900.

data.title: Explain addition and subtraction strategies
data.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
data.cluster: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to add and subtract.
data.description: Explain why addition and subtraction strategies work, using place value and the properties of operations.

data.title: Use addition and subtraction within 100 to solve word problems
data.cluster: Represent and solve problems involving addition and subtraction.
data.description: Use addition and subtraction within 100 to solve one- and two-step word problems involving situations of adding to, taking from, putting together, taking apart, and comparing, with unknowns in all positions, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

data.title: Fluently add and subtract within 20
data.description: Fluently add and subtract within 20 using mental strategies. By end of Grade 2, know from memory all sums of two one-digit numbers.

data.title: Determine odd or even numbers
data.cluster: Work with equal groups of objects to gain foundations for multiplication.
data.description: Determine whether a group of objects (up to 20) has an odd or even number of members, e.g., by pairing objects or counting them by 2s; write an equation to express an even number as a sum of two equal addends.

data.title: Use addition for rectangular arrays
data.cluster: Work with equal groups of objects to gain foundations for multiplication.
data.description: Use addition to find the total number of objects arranged in rectangular arrays with up to 5 rows and up to 5 columns; write an equation to express the total as a sum of equal addends.

data.title: Classify shapes by attributes
data.cluster: Reason with shapes and their attributes.
data.description: Understand that shapes in different categories (e.g., rhombuses, rectangles, and others) may share attributes (e.g., having four sides), and that the shared attributes can define a larger category (e.g., quadrilaterals). Recognize rhombuses, rectangles, and squares as examples of quadrilaterals, and draw examples of quadrilaterals that do not belong to any of these subcategories.

data.title: Partition shapes into parts with equal areas
data.cluster: Reason with shapes and their attributes.
data.description: Partition shapes into parts with equal areas. Express the area of each part as a unit fraction of the whole. For example, partition a shape into 4 parts with equal area, and describe the area of each part as 1/4 of the area of the shape.

data.title: Tell and write time and solve time interval problems
data.cluster: Solve problems involving measurement and estimation of intervals of time, liquid volumes, and masses of objects.
data.description: Tell and write time to the nearest minute and measure time intervals in minutes. Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of time intervals in minutes, e.g., by representing the problem on a number line diagram.

data.title: Measure and estimate liquid volumes and masses
data.cluster: Solve problems involving measurement and estimation of intervals of time, liquid volumes, and masses of objects.
data.description: Measure and estimate liquid volumes and masses of objects using standard units of grams (g), kilograms (kg), and liters (l). Add, subtract, multiply, or divide to solve one-step word problems involving masses or volumes that are given in the same units, e.g., by using drawings (such as a beaker with a measurement scale) to represent the problem.

data.title: Draw scaled picture and bar graphs
data.description: Draw a scaled picture graph and a scaled bar graph to represent a data set with several categories. Solve one- and two-step “how many more” and “how many less” problems using information presented in scaled bar graphs. For example, draw a bar graph in which each square in the bar graph might represent 5 pets.

data.title: Generate measurement data and make line plots
data.description: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths using rulers marked with halves and fourths of an inch. Show the data by making a line plot, where the horizontal scale is marked off in appropriate units—whole numbers, halves, or quarters.

data.title: Understand unit squares and area
data.cluster: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of area and relate area to multiplication and to addition.
data.description: A square with side length 1 unit, called “a unit square,” is said to have “one square unit” of area, and can be used to measure area.

data.title: Understand area of plane figures
data.cluster: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of area and relate area to multiplication and to addition.
data.description: A plane figure which can be covered without gaps or overlaps by n unit squares is said to have an area of n square units.

data.title: Measure areas by counting unit squares
data.cluster: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of area and relate area to multiplication and to addition.
data.description: Measure areas by counting unit squares (square cm, square m, square in, square ft, and improvised units).

data.title: Find area of rectangles by tiling
data.cluster: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of area and relate area to multiplication and to addition.
data.description: Find the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths by tiling it, and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths.

data.title: Multiply side lengths to find area of rectangles
data.cluster: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of area and relate area to multiplication and to addition.
data.description: Multiply side lengths to find areas of rectangles with whole-number side lengths in the context of solving real world and mathematical problems, and represent whole-number products as rectangular areas in mathematical reasoning.

data.title: Use area models for distributive property
data.cluster: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of area and relate area to multiplication and to addition.
data.description: Use tiling to show in a concrete case that the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths a and b + c is the sum of a × b and a × c. Use area models to represent the distributive property in mathematical reasoning.

data.title: Recognize area as additive and find area of rectilinear figures
data.cluster: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of area and relate area to multiplication and to addition.
data.description: Recognize area as additive. Find areas of rectilinear figures by decomposing them into non-overlapping rectangles and adding the areas of the non-overlapping parts, applying this technique to solve real world problems.

data.title: Solve problems involving perimeters
data.cluster: Geometric measurement: recognize perimeter as an attribute of plane figures and distinguish between linear and area measures.
data.description: Solve real world and mathematical problems involving perimeters of polygons, including finding the perimeter given the side lengths, finding an unknown side length, and exhibiting rectangles with the same perimeter and different areas or with the same area and different perimeters.

data.title: Round whole numbers to the nearest 10 or 100
data.cluster: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic.
data.description: Use place value understanding to round whole numbers to the nearest 10 or 100.

data.title: Fluently add and subtract within 1000
data.cluster: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic.
data.description: Fluently add and subtract within 1000 using strategies and algorithms based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.

data.title: Multiply one-digit whole numbers by multiples of 10
data.cluster: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic.
data.description: Multiply one-digit whole numbers by multiples of 10 in the range 10–90 (e.g., 9 × 80, 5 × 60) using strategies based on place value and properties of operations.

data.title: Understand fractions as parts of a whole
data.cluster: Develop understanding of fractions as numbers.
data.description: Understand a fraction 1/b as the quantity formed by 1 part when a whole is partitioned into b equal parts; understand a fraction a/b as the quantity formed by a parts of size 1/b.

data.title: Represent a fraction 1/b on a number line diagram
data.cluster: Develop understanding of fractions as numbers.
data.description: Represent a fraction 1/b on a number line diagram by defining the interval from 0 to 1 as the whole and partitioning it into b equal parts. Recognize that each part has size 1/b and that the endpoint of the part based at 0 locates the number 1/b on the number line.

data.title: Represent a fraction a/b on a number line diagram
data.cluster: Develop understanding of fractions as numbers.
data.description: Represent a fraction a/b on a number line diagram by marking off a lengths 1/b from 0. Recognize that the resulting interval has size a/b and that its endpoint locates the number a/b on the number line.

data.title: Understand equivalent fractions
data.cluster: Develop understanding of fractions as numbers.
data.description: Understand two fractions as equivalent (equal) if they are the same size, or the same point on a number line.

data.title: Recognize and generate simple equivalent fractions
data.cluster: Develop understanding of fractions as numbers.
data.description: Recognize and generate simple equivalent fractions, e.g., 1/2 = 2/4, 4/6 = 2/3. Explain why the fractions are equivalent, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

data.title: Express whole numbers as fractions
data.cluster: Develop understanding of fractions as numbers.
data.description: Express whole numbers as fractions, and recognize fractions that are equivalent to whole numbers. Examples: Express 3 in the form 3 = 3/1; recognize that 6/1 = 6; locate 4/4 and 1 at the same point of a number line diagram.

data.title: Compare two fractions with the same numerator or denominator
data.cluster: Develop understanding of fractions as numbers.
data.description: Compare two fractions with the same numerator or the same denominator by reasoning about their size.
