data.cluster: Understand congruence and similarity using physical models, transparencies, or geometry software.
data.description: Verify experimentally the properties of rotations, reflections, and translations: Parallel lines are taken to parallel lines.

data.title: Congruence via rigid motions
data.cluster: Understand congruence and similarity using physical models, transparencies, or geometry software.
data.description: Understand that a two-dimensional figure is congruent to another if the second can be obtained from the first by a sequence of rotations, reflections, and translations; given two congruent figures, describe a sequence that exhibits the congruence between them.

data.title: Coordinates and transformations
data.cluster: Understand congruence and similarity using physical models, transparencies, or geometry software.
data.description: Describe the effect of dilations, translations, rotations, and reflections on two-dimensional figures using coordinates.

data.title: Similarity via transformations
data.cluster: Understand congruence and similarity using physical models, transparencies, or geometry software.
data.description: Understand that a two-dimensional figure is similar to another if the second can be obtained from the first by a sequence of rotations, reflections, translations, and dilations; given two similar two-dimensional figures, describe a sequence that exhibits the similarity between them.

data.title: Angle arguments and similarity
data.cluster: Understand congruence and similarity using physical models, transparencies, or geometry software.
data.description: Use informal arguments to establish facts about the angle sum and exterior angle of triangles, about the angles created when parallel lines are cut by a transversal, and the angle-angle criterion for similarity of triangles. For example, arrange three copies of the same triangle so that the sum of the three angles appears to form a line, and give an argument in terms of transversals why this is so.

data.title: Proof of Pythagorean Theorem
data.cluster: Understand and apply the Pythagorean Theorem.
data.description: Explain a proof of the Pythagorean Theorem and its converse.

data.title: Applying Pythagorean Theorem
data.cluster: Understand and apply the Pythagorean Theorem.
data.description: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to determine unknown side lengths in right triangles in real-world and mathematical problems in two and three dimensions.

data.title: Distance in coordinate system
data.cluster: Understand and apply the Pythagorean Theorem.
data.description: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to find the distance between two points in a coordinate system.

data.title: Volumes of cones, cylinders, and spheres
data.cluster: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving volume of cylinders, cones, and spheres.
data.description: Know the formulas for the volumes of cones, cylinders, and spheres and use them to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

data.title: Know irrational numbers and decimal expansions
data.cluster: Know that there are numbers that are not rational, and approximate them by rational numbers.
data.description: Know that numbers that are not rational are called irrational. Understand informally that every number has a decimal expansion; for rational numbers show that the decimal expansion repeats eventually, and convert a decimal expansion which repeats eventually into a rational number.

data.title: Approximate irrational numbers
data.cluster: Know that there are numbers that are not rational, and approximate them by rational numbers.
data.description: Use rational approximations of irrational numbers to compare the size of irrational numbers, locate them approximately on a number line diagram, and estimate the value of expressions (e.g., π²). For example, by truncating the decimal expansion of √2, show that √2 is between 1 and 2, then between 1.4 and 1.5, and explain how to continue on to get better approximations.

data.title: Scatter plots and association
data.cluster: Investigate patterns of association in bivariate data.
data.description: Construct and interpret scatter plots for bivariate measurement data to investigate patterns of association between two quantities. Describe patterns such as clustering, outliers, positive or negative association, linear association, and nonlinear association.

data.title: Linear models for data
data.cluster: Investigate patterns of association in bivariate data.
data.description: Know that straight lines are widely used to model relationships between two quantitative variables. For scatter plots that suggest a linear association, informally fit a straight line, and informally assess the model fit by judging the closeness of the data points to the line.

data.title: Interpreting linear models
data.cluster: Investigate patterns of association in bivariate data.
data.description: Use the equation of a linear model to solve problems in the context of bivariate measurement data, interpreting the slope and intercept. For example, in a linear model for a biology experiment, interpret a slope of 1.5 cm/hr as meaning that an additional hour of sunlight each day is associated with an additional 1.5 cm in mature plant height.

data.title: Bivariate categorical data
data.cluster: Investigate patterns of association in bivariate data.
data.description: Understand that patterns of association can also be seen in bivariate categorical data by displaying frequencies and relative frequencies in a two-way table. Construct and interpret a two-way table summarizing data on two categorical variables collected from the same subjects. Use relative frequencies calculated for rows or columns to describe possible association between the two variables. For example, collect data from students in your class on whether or not they have a curfew on school nights and whether or not they have assigned chores at home. Is there evidence that those who have a curfew also tend to have chores?

data.title: A-APR.1
data.description: Understand that polynomials form a system analogous to the integers, namely, they are closed under the operations of addition, subtraction, and multiplication; add, subtract, and multiply polynomials.

data.title: A-APR.2
data.cluster: Understand the relationship between zeros and factors of polynomials
data.description: Know and apply the Remainder Theorem: For a polynomial p(x) and a number a, the remainder on division by x – a is p(a), so p(a) = 0 if and only if (x – a) is a factor of p(x).

data.title: A-APR.3
data.cluster: Understand the relationship between zeros and factors of polynomials
data.description: Identify zeros of polynomials when suitable factorizations are available, and use the zeros to construct a rough graph of the function defined by the polynomial.

data.title: A-APR.4
data.cluster: Use polynomial identities to solve problems
data.description: Prove polynomial identities and use them to describe numerical relationships. For example, the polynomial identity (x2 + y2)2 = (x2 – y2)2 + (2xy)2 can be used to generate Pythagorean triples.

data.title: A-APR.5
data.cluster: Use polynomial identities to solve problems
data.description: (+) Know and apply the Binomial Theorem for the expansion of (x + y)n in powers of x and y for a positive integer n, where x and y are any numbers, with coefficients determined for example by Pascal’s Triangle.

data.title: A-APR.6
data.description: Rewrite simple rational expressions in different forms; write a(x)/b(x) in the form q(x) + r(x)/b(x), where a(x), b(x), q(x), and r(x) are polynomials with the degree of r(x) less than the degree of b(x), using inspection, long division, or, for the more complicated examples, a computer algebra system.

data.title: A-APR.7
data.description: (+) Understand that rational expressions form a system analogous to the rational numbers, closed under addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division by a nonzero rational expression; add, subtract, multiply, and divide rational expressions.

data.title: A-CED.1
data.cluster: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships
data.description: Create equations and inequalities in one variable and use them to solve problems. Include equations arising from linear and quadratic functions, and simple rational and exponential functions.

data.title: A-CED.2
data.cluster: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships
data.description: Create equations in two or more variables to represent relationships between quantities; graph equations on coordinate axes with labels and scales.

data.title: A-CED.3
data.cluster: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships
data.description: Represent constraints by equations or inequalities, and by systems of equations and/or inequalities, and interpret solutions as viable or non-viable options in a modeling context. For example, represent inequalities describing nutritional and cost constraints on combinations of different foods.

data.title: A-CED.4
data.cluster: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships
data.description: Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest, using the same reasoning as in solving equations. For example, rearrange Ohm’s law V = IR to highlight resistance R.

data.title: A-REI.1
data.cluster: Understand solving equations as a process of reasoning and explain the reasoning
data.description: Explain each step in solving a simple equation as following from the equality of numbers asserted at the previous step, starting from the assumption that the original equation has a solution. Construct a viable argument to justify a solution method.

data.title: A-REI.10
data.cluster: Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically
data.description: Understand that the graph of an equation in two variables is the set of all its solutions plotted in the coordinate plane, often forming a curve (which could be a line).

data.title: A-REI.11
data.cluster: Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically
data.description: Explain why the x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of the equations y = f(x) and y = g(x) intersect are the solutions of the equation f(x) = g(x); find the solutions approximately, e.g., using technology to graph the functions, make tables of values, or find successive approximations. Include cases where f(x) and/or g(x) are linear, polynomial, rational, absolute value, exponential, and logarithmic functions.★

data.title: A-REI.12
data.cluster: Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically
data.description: Graph the solutions to a linear inequality in two variables as a half-plane (excluding the boundary in the case of a strict inequality), and graph the solution set to a system of linear inequalities in two variables as the intersection of the corresponding half-planes.

data.title: A-REI.2
data.cluster: Understand solving equations as a process of reasoning and explain the reasoning
data.description: Solve simple rational and radical equations in one variable, and give examples showing how extraneous solutions may arise.

data.title: A-REI.3
data.cluster: Solve equations and inequalities in one variable
data.description: Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable, including equations with coefficients represented by letters.

data.title: A-REI.4
data.cluster: Solve equations and inequalities in one variable
data.description: Solve quadratic equations in one variable.

data.title: A-REI.4.a
data.cluster: Solve equations and inequalities in one variable
data.description: Use the method of completing the square to transform any quadratic equation in x into an equation of the form (x – p)2 = q that has the same solutions. Derive the quadratic formula from this form.

data.title: A-REI.4.b
data.cluster: Solve equations and inequalities in one variable
data.description: Solve quadratic equations by inspection (e.g., for x2 = 49), taking square roots, completing the square, the quadratic formula and factoring, as appropriate to the initial form of the equation. Recognize when the quadratic formula gives complex solutions and write them as a ± bi for real numbers a and b.

data.title: A-REI.5
data.description: Prove that, given a system of two equations in two variables, replacing one equation by the sum of that equation and a multiple of the other produces a system with the same solutions.

data.title: A-REI.6
data.description: Solve systems of linear equations exactly and approximately (e.g., with graphs), focusing on pairs of linear equations in two variables.

data.title: A-REI.7
data.description: Solve a simple system consisting of a linear equation and a quadratic equation in two variables algebraically and graphically. For example, find the points of intersection between the line y = –3x and the circle x2 + y2 = 3.

data.title: A-REI.8
data.description: (+) Represent a system of linear equations as a single matrix equation in a vector variable.

data.title: A-REI.9
data.description: (+) Find the inverse of a matrix if it exists and use it to solve systems of linear equations (using technology for matrices of dimension 3 × 3 or greater).

data.title: A-SSE.1
data.description: Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context.★

data.title: A-SSE.1.a
data.description: Interpret parts of an expression, such as terms, factors, and coefficients.

data.title: A-SSE.1.b
data.description: Interpret complicated expressions by viewing one or more of their parts as a single entity. For example, interpret P(1+r)n as the product of P and a factor not depending on P.

data.title: A-SSE.2
data.description: Use the structure of an expression to identify ways to rewrite it. For example, see x4 – y4 as (x2)2 – (y2)2, thus recognizing it as a difference of squares that can be factored as (x2 – y2)(x2 + y2).

data.title: A-SSE.3
data.cluster: Write expressions in equivalent forms to solve problems
data.description: Choose and produce an equivalent form of an expression to reveal and explain properties of the quantity represented by the expression.★

data.title: A-SSE.3.a
data.cluster: Write expressions in equivalent forms to solve problems
data.description: Factor a quadratic expression to reveal the zeros of the function it defines.

data.title: A-SSE.3.b
data.cluster: Write expressions in equivalent forms to solve problems
data.description: Complete the square in a quadratic expression to reveal the maximum or minimum value of the function it defines.

data.title: A-SSE.3.c
data.cluster: Write expressions in equivalent forms to solve problems
data.description: Use the properties of exponents to transform expressions for exponential functions. For example the expression 1.15t can be rewritten as (1.151/12)12t ≈ 1.01212t to reveal the approximate equivalent monthly interest rate if the annual rate is 15%.

data.title: A-SSE.4
data.cluster: Write expressions in equivalent forms to solve problems
data.description: Derive the formula for the sum of a finite geometric series (when the common ratio is not 1), and use the formula to solve problems. For example, calculate mortgage payments.★

data.title: Determine Explicit Expression or Recursive Process
data.cluster: Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities
data.description: Determine an explicit expression, a recursive process, or steps for calculation from a context.

data.title: Combine Standard Function Types
data.cluster: Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities
data.description: Combine standard function types using arithmetic operations. For example, build a function that models the temperature of a cooling body by adding a constant function to a decaying exponential, and relate these functions to the model.

data.title: Compose Functions
data.cluster: Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities
data.description: (+) Compose functions. For example, if T(y) is the temperature in the atmosphere as a function of height, and h(t) is the height of a weather balloon as a function of time, then T(h(t)) is the temperature at the location of the weather balloon as a function of time.

data.title: Write Arithmetic and Geometric Sequences
data.cluster: Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities
data.description: Write arithmetic and geometric sequences both recursively and with an explicit formula, use them to model situations, and translate between the two forms.★

data.title: Identify Effects of Transformations on Graphs
data.cluster: Build new functions from existing functions
data.description: Identify the effect on the graph of replacing f(x) by f(x) + k, k f(x), f(kx), and f(x + k) for specific values of k (both positive and negative); find the value of k given the graphs. Experiment with cases and illustrate an explanation of the effects on the graph using technology. Include recognizing even and odd functions from their graphs and algebraic expressions for them.

data.title: Solve for Inverse Function
data.cluster: Build new functions from existing functions
data.description: Solve an equation of the form f(x) = c for a simple function f that has an inverse and write an expression for the inverse. For example, f(x) =2 x³ or f(x) = (x+1)/(x–1) for x ≠ 1.

data.title: Verify Inverse Functions by Composition
data.cluster: Build new functions from existing functions
data.description: (+) Verify by composition that one function is the inverse of another.

data.title: Read Inverse Values from Graph or Table
data.cluster: Build new functions from existing functions
data.description: (+) Read values of an inverse function from a graph or a table, given that the function has an inverse.

data.title: Produce Invertible Function by Restricting Domain
data.cluster: Build new functions from existing functions
data.description: (+) Produce an invertible function from a non-invertible function by restricting the domain.

data.title: Understand Inverse Relationship of Exponents and Logarithms
data.cluster: Build new functions from existing functions
data.description: (+) Understand the inverse relationship between exponents and logarithms and use this relationship to solve problems involving logarithms and exponents.

data.title: Understand Function Definition and Graph
data.cluster: Understand the concept of a function and use function notation
data.description: Understand that a function from one set (called the domain) to another set (called the range) assigns to each element of the domain exactly one element of the range. If f is a function and x is an element of its domain, then f(x) denotes the output of f corresponding to the input x. The graph of f is the graph of the equation y = f(x).

data.title: Use Function Notation
data.cluster: Understand the concept of a function and use function notation
data.description: Use function notation, evaluate functions for inputs in their domains, and interpret statements that use function notation in terms of a context.

data.title: Sequences as Functions
data.cluster: Understand the concept of a function and use function notation
data.description: Recognize that sequences are functions, sometimes defined recursively, whose domain is a subset of the integers. For example, the Fibonacci sequence is defined recursively by f(0) = f(1) = 1, f(n+1) = f(n) + f(n-1) for n ≥ 1.

data.title: Interpret Key Features of Functions
data.cluster: Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context
data.description: For a function that models a relationship between two quantities, interpret key features of graphs and tables in terms of the quantities, and sketch graphs showing key features given a verbal description of the relationship. Key features include: intercepts; intervals where the function is increasing, decreasing, positive, or negative; relative maximums and minimums; symmetries; end behavior; and periodicity.★

data.title: Relate Domain to Context
data.cluster: Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context
data.description: Relate the domain of a function to its graph and, where applicable, to the quantitative relationship it describes. For example, if the function h(n) gives the number of person-hours it takes to assemble n engines in a factory, then the positive integers would be an appropriate domain for the function.★

data.title: Calculate Average Rate of Change
data.cluster: Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context
data.description: Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a function (presented symbolically or as a table) over a specified interval. Estimate the rate of change from a graph.★

data.title: Graph Linear and Quadratic Functions
data.description: Graph linear and quadratic functions and show intercepts, maxima, and minima.

data.title: Graph Square Root, Cube Root, and Piecewise Functions
data.description: Graph square root, cube root, and piecewise-defined functions, including step functions and absolute value functions.

data.title: Graph Polynomial Functions
data.description: Graph polynomial functions, identifying zeros when suitable factorizations are available, and showing end behavior.

data.title: Graph Rational Functions
data.description: (+) Graph rational functions, identifying zeros and asymptotes when suitable factorizations are available, and showing end behavior.

data.title: Graph Exponential, Logarithmic, and Trigonometric Functions
data.description: Graph exponential and logarithmic functions, showing intercepts and end behavior, and trigonometric functions, showing period, midline, and amplitude.

data.title: Factor and Complete the Square in Quadratic Functions
data.description: Use the process of factoring and completing the square in a quadratic function to show zeros, extreme values, and symmetry of the graph, and interpret these in terms of a context.

data.title: Interpret Expressions for Exponential Functions
data.description: Use the properties of exponents to interpret expressions for exponential functions. For example, identify percent rate of change in functions such as y = (1.02)ᵗ, y = (0.97)ᵗ, y = (1.01)¹²ᵗ, y = (1.2)ᵗ/¹⁰, and classify them as representing exponential growth or decay.

data.title: Compare Functions Represented Differently
data.description: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions). For example, given a graph of one quadratic function and an algebraic expression for another, say which has the larger maximum.

data.title: Prove Growth of Linear and Exponential Functions
data.cluster: Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems
data.description: Prove that linear functions grow by equal differences over equal intervals, and that exponential functions grow by equal factors over equal intervals.

data.title: Recognize Constant Rate of Change
data.cluster: Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems
data.description: Recognize situations in which one quantity changes at a constant rate per unit interval relative to another.

data.title: Recognize Constant Percent Rate
data.cluster: Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems
data.description: Recognize situations in which a quantity grows or decays by a constant percent rate per unit interval relative to another.

data.title: Construct Linear and Exponential Functions
data.cluster: Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems
data.description: Construct linear and exponential functions, including arithmetic and geometric sequences, given a graph, a description of a relationship, or two input-output pairs (include reading these from a table).

data.title: Compare Growth of Exponential and Polynomial Functions
data.cluster: Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems
data.description: Observe using graphs and tables that a quantity increasing exponentially eventually exceeds a quantity increasing linearly, quadratically, or (more generally) as a polynomial function.

data.title: Express Exponential Models as Logarithms
data.cluster: Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems
data.description: For exponential models, express as a logarithm the solution to abᶜᵗ = d where a, c, and d are numbers and the base b is 2, 10, or e; evaluate the logarithm using technology.

data.title: Interpret Parameters in Linear or Exponential Functions
data.cluster: Interpret expressions for functions in terms of the situation they model
data.description: Interpret the parameters in a linear or exponential function in terms of a context.

data.title: Understand Radian Measure
data.cluster: Extend the domain of trigonometric functions using the unit circle
data.description: Understand radian measure of an angle as the length of the arc on the unit circle subtended by the angle.

data.title: Extend Trigonometric Functions Using Unit Circle
data.cluster: Extend the domain of trigonometric functions using the unit circle
data.description: Explain how the unit circle in the coordinate plane enables the extension of trigonometric functions to all real numbers, interpreted as radian measures of angles traversed counterclockwise around the unit circle.

data.title: Use Special Triangles and Unit Circle
data.cluster: Extend the domain of trigonometric functions using the unit circle
data.description: (+) Use special triangles to determine geometrically the values of sine, cosine, tangent for π/3, π/4 and π/6, and use the unit circle to express the values of sine, cosine, and tangent for π–x, π+x, and 2π–x in terms of their values for x, where x is any real number.

data.title: Explain Symmetry and Periodicity
data.cluster: Extend the domain of trigonometric functions using the unit circle
data.description: (+) Use the unit circle to explain symmetry (odd and even) and periodicity of trigonometric functions.

data.title: Model Periodic Phenomena
data.cluster: Model periodic phenomena with trigonometric functions
data.description: Choose trigonometric functions to model periodic phenomena with specified amplitude, frequency, and midline.★

data.title: Restrict Domain to Construct Inverse
data.cluster: Model periodic phenomena with trigonometric functions
data.description: (+) Understand that restricting a trigonometric function to a domain on which it is always increasing or always decreasing allows its inverse to be constructed.

data.title: Use Inverse Functions to Solve Equations
data.cluster: Model periodic phenomena with trigonometric functions
data.description: (+) Use inverse functions to solve trigonometric equations that arise in modeling contexts; evaluate the solutions using technology, and interpret them in terms of the context.★

data.title: Prove and Use Pythagorean Identity
data.description: Prove the Pythagorean identity sin²(θ) + cos²(θ) = 1 and use it to find sin(θ), cos(θ), or tan(θ) given sin(θ), cos(θ), or tan(θ) and the quadrant of the angle.

data.title: Prove Addition and Subtraction Formulas
data.description: (+) Prove the addition and subtraction formulas for sine, cosine, and tangent and use them to solve problems.

data.title: Similarity of Circles
data.cluster: Understand and apply theorems about circles
data.description: Prove that all circles are similar.

data.title: Relationships Among Angles, Radii, and Chords
data.cluster: Understand and apply theorems about circles
data.description: Identify and describe relationships among inscribed angles, radii, and chords. Include the relationship between central, inscribed, and circumscribed angles; inscribed angles on a diameter are right angles; the radius of a circle is perpendicular to the tangent where the radius intersects the circle.

data.title: Inscribed and Circumscribed Circles
data.cluster: Understand and apply theorems about circles
data.description: Construct the inscribed and circumscribed circles of a triangle, and prove properties of angles for a quadrilateral inscribed in a circle.

data.title: Construct Tangent Line
data.cluster: Understand and apply theorems about circles
data.description: (+) Construct a tangent line from a point outside a given circle to the circle.

data.title: Arc Length and Area of Sectors
data.cluster: Find arc lengths and areas of sectors of circles
data.description: Derive using similarity the fact that the length of the arc intercepted by an angle is proportional to the radius, and define the radian measure of the angle as the constant of proportionality; derive the formula for the area of a sector.

data.title: Know Precise Definitions of Geometric Terms
data.cluster: Experiment with transformations in the plane
data.description: Know precise definitions of angle, circle, perpendicular line, parallel line, and line segment, based on the undefined notions of point, line, distance along a line, and distance around a circular arc.

data.title: Represent and Compare Transformations
data.cluster: Experiment with transformations in the plane
data.description: Represent transformations in the plane using, e.g., transparencies and geometry software; describe transformations as functions that take points in the plane as inputs and give other points as outputs. Compare transformations that preserve distance and angle to those that do not (e.g., translation versus horizontal stretch).

data.title: Symmetries of Basic Polygons
data.cluster: Experiment with transformations in the plane
data.description: Given a rectangle, parallelogram, trapezoid, or regular polygon, describe the rotations and reflections that carry it onto itself.

data.title: Develop Definitions of Rigid Motions
data.cluster: Experiment with transformations in the plane
data.description: Develop definitions of rotations, reflections, and translations in terms of angles, circles, perpendicular lines, parallel lines, and line segments.

data.title: Draw Transformed Figures
data.cluster: Experiment with transformations in the plane
data.description: Given a geometric figure and a rotation, reflection, or translation, draw the transformed figure using, e.g., graph paper, tracing paper, or geometry software. Specify a sequence of transformations that will carry a given figure onto another.

data.title: Rigid Motions and Congruence
data.cluster: Understand congruence in terms of rigid motions
data.description: Use geometric descriptions of rigid motions to transform figures and to predict the effect of a given rigid motion on a given figure; given two figures, use the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions to decide if they are congruent.

data.title: Triangle Congruence and Rigid Motions
data.cluster: Understand congruence in terms of rigid motions
data.description: Use the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions to show that two triangles are congruent if and only if corresponding pairs of sides and corresponding pairs of angles are congruent.

data.title: Explain Triangle Congruence Criteria
data.cluster: Understand congruence in terms of rigid motions
data.description: Explain how the criteria for triangle congruence (ASA, SAS, and SSS) follow from the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions.

data.title: Prove Theorems About Triangles
data.description: Prove theorems about triangles. Theorems include: measures of interior angles of a triangle sum to 180°; base angles of isosceles triangles are congruent; the segment joining midpoints of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and half the length; the medians of a triangle meet at a point.

data.title: Prove Theorems About Parallelograms
data.description: Prove theorems about parallelograms. Theorems include: opposite sides are congruent, opposite angles are congruent, the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, and conversely, rectangles are parallelograms with congruent diagonals.

data.title: Prove Theorems About Lines and Angles
data.description: Prove theorems about lines and angles. Theorems include: vertical angles are congruent; when a transversal crosses parallel lines, alternate interior angles are congruent and corresponding angles are congruent; points on a perpendicular bisector of a line segment are exactly those equidistant from the segment’s endpoints.

data.title: Make Formal Geometric Constructions
data.description: Make formal geometric constructions with a variety of tools and methods (compass and straightedge, string, reflective devices, paper folding, dynamic geometric software, etc.). Copying a segment; copying an angle; bisecting a segment; bisecting an angle; constructing perpendicular lines, including the perpendicular bisector of a line segment; and constructing a line parallel to a given line through a point not on the line.

data.title: Construct Inscribed Polygons
data.description: Construct an equilateral triangle, a square, and a regular hexagon inscribed in a circle.

data.title: Arguments for Area and Volume Formulas
data.cluster: Explain volume formulas and use them to solve problems
data.description: Give an informal argument for the formulas for the circumference of a circle, area of a circle, volume of a cylinder, pyramid, and cone. Use dissection arguments, Cavalieri’s principle, and informal limit arguments.

data.title: Volume Formulas for Sphere and Other Solids
data.cluster: Explain volume formulas and use them to solve problems
data.description: (+) Give an informal argument using Cavalieri’s principle for the formulas for the volume of a sphere and other solid figures.

data.title: Use Volume Formulas
data.cluster: Explain volume formulas and use them to solve problems
data.description: Use volume formulas for cylinders, pyramids, cones, and spheres to solve problems.

data.title: Cross-Sections and Rotations
data.cluster: Visualize relationships between two-dimensional and three-dimensional objects
data.description: Identify the shapes of two-dimensional cross-sections of three-dimensional objects, and identify three-dimensional objects generated by rotations of two-dimensional objects.

data.title: Derive Equation of a Circle
data.cluster: Translate between the geometric description and the equation for a conic section
data.description: Derive the equation of a circle of given center and radius using the Pythagorean Theorem; complete the square to find the center and radius of a circle given by an equation.

data.title: Derive Equation of a Parabola
data.cluster: Translate between the geometric description and the equation for a conic section
data.description: Derive the equation of a parabola given a focus and directrix.

data.title: Derive Equations of Ellipses and Hyperbolas
data.cluster: Translate between the geometric description and the equation for a conic section
data.description: (+) Derive the equations of ellipses and hyperbolas given the foci, using the fact that the sum or difference of distances from the foci is constant.

data.title: Prove Geometric Theorems Algebraically
data.cluster: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically
data.description: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically. For example, prove or disprove that a figure defined by four given points in the coordinate plane is a rectangle; prove or disprove that the point (1, √3) lies on the circle centered at the origin and containing the point (0, 2).

data.title: Slope Criteria for Parallel and Perpendicular Lines
data.cluster: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically
data.description: Prove the slope criteria for parallel and perpendicular lines and use them to solve geometric problems (e.g., find the equation of a line parallel or perpendicular to a given line that passes through a given point).

data.title: Partition a Line Segment
data.cluster: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically
data.description: Find the point on a directed line segment between two given points that partitions the segment in a given ratio.

data.title: Compute Perimeters and Areas Using Coordinates
data.cluster: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically
data.description: Use coordinates to compute perimeters of polygons and areas of triangles and rectangles, e.g., using the distance formula.

data.title: Use Geometric Shapes to Describe Objects
data.cluster: Apply geometric concepts in modeling situations
data.description: Use geometric shapes, their measures, and their properties to describe objects (e.g., modeling a tree trunk or a human torso as a cylinder).

data.title: Apply Concepts of Density
data.cluster: Apply geometric concepts in modeling situations
data.description: Apply concepts of density based on area and volume in modeling situations (e.g., persons per square mile, BTUs per cubic foot).

data.title: Solve Design Problems
data.cluster: Apply geometric concepts in modeling situations
data.description: Apply geometric methods to solve design problems (e.g., designing an object or structure to satisfy physical constraints or minimize cost; working with typographic grid systems based on ratios).

data.title: Verify Properties of Dilations
data.cluster: Understand similarity in terms of similarity transformations
data.description: Verify experimentally the properties of dilations given by a center and a scale factor.

data.title: Dilations and Lines
data.cluster: Understand similarity in terms of similarity transformations
data.description: A dilation takes a line not passing through the center of the dilation to a parallel line, and leaves a line passing through the center unchanged.

data.title: Dilations and Line Segments
data.cluster: Understand similarity in terms of similarity transformations
data.description: The dilation of a line segment is longer or shorter in the ratio given by the scale factor.

data.title: Similarity Transformations and Triangle Similarity
data.cluster: Understand similarity in terms of similarity transformations
data.description: Given two figures, use the definition of similarity in terms of similarity transformations to decide if they are similar; explain using similarity transformations the meaning of similarity for triangles as the equality of all corresponding pairs of angles and the proportionality of all corresponding pairs of sides.

data.title: Establish AA Similarity Criterion
data.cluster: Understand similarity in terms of similarity transformations
data.description: Use the properties of similarity transformations to establish the AA criterion for two triangles to be similar.

data.title: Prove Theorems About Triangles Involving Similarity
data.description: Prove theorems about triangles. Theorems include: a line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two proportionally, and conversely; the Pythagorean Theorem proved using triangle similarity.

data.title: Use Congruence and Similarity Criteria
data.description: Use congruence and similarity criteria for triangles to solve problems and to prove relationships in geometric figures.

data.title: Define Trigonometric Ratios
data.cluster: Define trigonometric ratios and solve problems involving right triangles
data.description: Understand that by similarity, side ratios in right triangles are properties of the angles in the triangle, leading to definitions of trigonometric ratios for acute angles.

data.title: Sine and Cosine of Complementary Angles
data.cluster: Define trigonometric ratios and solve problems involving right triangles
data.description: Explain and use the relationship between the sine and cosine of complementary angles.

data.title: Solve Right Triangles
data.cluster: Define trigonometric ratios and solve problems involving right triangles
data.description: Use trigonometric ratios and the Pythagorean Theorem to solve right triangles in applied problems.

data.title: Prove Laws of Sines and Cosines
data.description: (+) Prove the Laws of Sines and Cosines and use them to solve problems.

data.title: Apply Laws of Sines and Cosines
data.description: (+) Understand and apply the Law of Sines and the Law of Cosines to find unknown measurements in right and non-right triangles (e.g., surveying problems, resultant forces).

data.title: Derive Area Formula for Triangle
data.description: (+) Derive the formula A = 1/2 ab sin(C) for the area of a triangle by drawing an auxiliary line from a vertex perpendicular to the opposite side.

data.title: Count to 100 by Ones and Tens
data.cluster: Know number names and the count sequence.
data.description: Count to 100 by ones and by tens.

data.title: Count Forward From a Given Number
data.cluster: Know number names and the count sequence.
data.description: Count forward beginning from a given number within the known sequence (instead of having to begin at 1).

data.title: Write Numbers 0 to 20
data.cluster: Know number names and the count sequence.
data.description: Write numbers from 0 to 20. Represent a number of objects with a written numeral 0-20 (with 0 representing a count of no objects).

data.title: Relationship Between Numbers and Quantities
data.cluster: Count to tell the number of objects.
data.description: Understand the relationship between numbers and quantities; connect counting to cardinality.

data.title: One-to-One Correspondence
data.cluster: Count to tell the number of objects.
data.description: When counting objects, say the number names in the standard order, pairing each object with one and only one number name and each number name with one and only one object.

data.title: Last Number Represents Quantity
data.cluster: Count to tell the number of objects.
data.description: Understand that the last number name said tells the number of objects counted. The number of objects is the same regardless of their arrangement or the order in which they were counted.

data.title: Successive Numbers Increase Quantity
data.cluster: Count to tell the number of objects.
data.description: Understand that each successive number name refers to a quantity that is one larger.

data.title: Count to Answer How Many
data.cluster: Count to tell the number of objects.
data.description: Count to answer “how many?” questions about as many as 20 things arranged in a line, a rectangular array, or a circle, or as many as 10 things in a scattered configuration; given a number from 1–20, count out that many objects.

data.title: Compare Groups of Objects
data.description: Identify whether the number of objects in one group is greater than, less than, or equal to the number of objects in another group, e.g., by using matching and counting strategies.

data.title: Compare Written Numerals
data.description: Compare two numbers between 1 and 10 presented as written numerals.

data.title: Describe Objects Using Shape Names and Position
data.cluster: Identify and describe shapes (squares, circles, triangles, rectangles, hexagons, cubes, cones, cylinders, and spheres).
data.description: Describe objects in the environment using names of shapes, and describe the relative positions of these objects using terms such as above, below, beside, in front of, behind, and next to.

data.title: Name Shapes Correctly
data.cluster: Identify and describe shapes (squares, circles, triangles, rectangles, hexagons, cubes, cones, cylinders, and spheres).
data.description: Correctly name shapes regardless of their orientations or overall size.

data.title: Identify Two-Dimensional and Three-Dimensional Shapes
data.cluster: Identify and describe shapes (squares, circles, triangles, rectangles, hexagons, cubes, cones, cylinders, and spheres).
data.description: Identify shapes as two-dimensional (lying in a plane, “flat”) or three-dimensional (“solid”).

data.title: Analyze and Compare Shapes
data.cluster: Analyze, compare, create, and compose shapes.
data.description: Analyze and compare two- and three-dimensional shapes, in different sizes and orientations, using informal language to describe their similarities, differences, parts (e.g., number of sides and vertices/“corners”) and other attributes (e.g., having sides of equal length).

data.title: Model Shapes in the World
data.cluster: Analyze, compare, create, and compose shapes.
data.description: Model shapes in the world by building shapes from components (e.g., sticks and clay balls) and drawing shapes.

data.title: Compose Simple Shapes
data.cluster: Analyze, compare, create, and compose shapes.
data.description: Compose simple shapes to form larger shapes. For example, “Can you join these two triangles with full sides touching to make a rectangle?”

data.title: Describe Measurable Attributes
data.description: Describe measurable attributes of objects, such as length or weight. Describe several measurable attributes of a single object.

data.title: Compare Objects with Measurable Attributes
data.description: Directly compare two objects with a measurable attribute in common, to see which object has “more of”/“less of” the attribute, and describe the difference. For example, directly compare the heights of two children and describe one child as taller/shorter.

data.title: Classify and Count Objects
data.cluster: Classify objects and count the number of objects in each category.
data.description: Classify objects into given categories; count the numbers of objects in each category and sort the categories by count.

data.title: Compose and Decompose Numbers 11-19
data.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
data.cluster: Work with numbers 11–19 to gain foundations for place value.
data.description: Compose and decompose numbers from 11 to 19 into ten ones and some further ones, e.g., by using objects or drawings, and record each composition or decomposition by a drawing or equation (e.g., 18 = 10 + 8); understand that these numbers are composed of ten ones and one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine ones.

data.title: Represent Addition and Subtraction
data.cluster: Understand addition as putting together and adding to, and understand subtraction as taking apart and taking from.
data.description: Represent addition and subtraction with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds (e.g., claps), acting out situations, verbal explanations, expressions, or equations.

data.title: Solve Addition and Subtraction Word Problems
data.cluster: Understand addition as putting together and adding to, and understand subtraction as taking apart and taking from.
data.description: Solve addition and subtraction word problems, and add and subtract within 10, e.g., by using objects or drawings to represent the problem.

data.title: Decompose Numbers Less Than or Equal to 10
data.cluster: Understand addition as putting together and adding to, and understand subtraction as taking apart and taking from.
data.description: Decompose numbers less than or equal to 10 into pairs in more than one way, e.g., by using objects or drawings, and record each decomposition by a drawing or equation (e.g., 5 = 2 + 3 and 5 = 4 + 1).

data.title: Make 10
data.cluster: Understand addition as putting together and adding to, and understand subtraction as taking apart and taking from.
data.description: For any number from 1 to 9, find the number that makes 10 when added to the given number, e.g., by using objects or drawings, and record the answer with a drawing or equation.

data.title: Fluently Add and Subtract Within 5
data.cluster: Understand addition as putting together and adding to, and understand subtraction as taking apart and taking from.
data.description: Fluently add and subtract within 5.

data.title: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them
data.description: Mathematically proficient students start by explaining to themselves the meaning of a problem and looking for entry points to its solution. They analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. They make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution and plan a solution pathway rather than simply jumping into a solution attempt. They consider analogous problems, and try special cases and simpler forms of the original problem in order to gain insight into its solution. They monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Older students might, depending on the context of the problem, transform algebraic expressions or change the viewing window on their graphing calculator to get the information they need. Mathematically proficient students can explain correspondences between equations, verbal descriptions, tables, and graphs or draw diagrams of important features and relationships, graph data, and search for regularity or trends. Younger students might rely on using concrete objects or pictures to help conceptualize and solve a problem. Mathematically proficient students check their answers to problems using a different method, and they continually ask themselves, “Does this make sense?” They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.

data.title: Reason abstractly and quantitatively
data.description: Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. They bring two complementary abilities to bear on problems involving quantitative relationships: the ability to decontextualize—to abstract a given situation and represent it symbolically and manipulate the representing symbols as if they have a life of their own, without necessarily attending to their referents—and the ability to contextualize, to pause as needed during the manipulation process in order to probe into the referents for the symbols involved. Quantitative reasoning entails habits of creating a coherent representation of the problem at hand; considering the units involved; attending to the meaning of quantities, not just how to compute them; and knowing and flexibly using different properties of operations and objects.

data.title: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others
data.description: Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.

data.title: Model with mathematics
data.description: Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

data.title: Use appropriate tools strategically
data.description: Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

data.title: Attend to precision
data.description: Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

data.title: Look for and make use of structure
data.description: Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. Young students, for example, might notice that three and seven more is the same amount as seven and three more, or they may sort a collection of shapes according to how many sides the shapes have. Later, students will see 7 × 8 equals the well remembered 7 × 5 + 7 × 3, in preparation for learning about the distributive property. In the expression x² + 9x + 14, older students can see the 14 as 2 × 7 and the 9 as 2 + 7. They recognize the significance of an existing line in a geometric figure and can use the strategy of drawing an auxiliary line for solving problems. They also can step back for an overview and shift perspective. They can see complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects. For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.

data.title: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning
data.description: Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Upper elementary students might notice when dividing 25 by 11 that they are repeating the same calculations over and over again, and conclude they have a repeating decimal. By paying attention to the calculation of slope as they repeatedly check whether points are on the line through (1, 2) with slope 3, middle school students might abstract the equation (y – 2)/(x – 1) = 3. Noticing the regularity in the way terms cancel when expanding (x – 1)(x + 1), (x – 1)(x² + x + 1), and (x – 1)(x³ + x² + x + 1) might lead them to the general formula for the sum of a geometric series. As they work to solve a problem, mathematically proficient students maintain oversight of the process, while attending to the details. They continually evaluate the reasonableness of their intermediate results.

data.title: N-CN.1
data.cluster: Perform arithmetic operations with complex numbers.
data.description: Know there is a complex number i such that i^2 = –1, and every complex number has the form a + bi with a and b real.

data.title: N-CN.2
data.cluster: Perform arithmetic operations with complex numbers.
data.description: Use the relation i^2 = –1 and the commutative, associative, and distributive properties to add, subtract, and multiply complex numbers.

data.title: N-CN.3
data.cluster: Perform arithmetic operations with complex numbers.
data.description: (+) Find the conjugate of a complex number; use conjugates to find moduli and quotients of complex numbers.

data.title: N-CN.4
data.cluster: Represent complex numbers and their operations on the complex plane.
data.description: (+) Represent complex numbers on the complex plane in rectangular and polar form (including real and imaginary numbers), and explain why the rectangular and polar forms of a given complex number represent the same number.

data.title: N-CN.5
data.cluster: Represent complex numbers and their operations on the complex plane.
data.description: (+) Represent addition, subtraction, multiplication, and conjugation of complex numbers geometrically on the complex plane; use properties of this representation for computation. For example, (–1 + √3 i)^3 = 8 because (–1 + √3 i) has modulus 2 and argument 120°.

data.title: N-CN.6
data.cluster: Represent complex numbers and their operations on the complex plane.
data.description: (+) Calculate the distance between numbers in the complex plane as the modulus of the difference, and the midpoint of a segment as the average of the numbers at its endpoints.

data.title: N-CN.7
data.cluster: Use complex numbers in polynomial identities and equations.
data.description: Solve quadratic equations with real coefficients that have complex solutions.

data.title: N-CN.8
data.cluster: Use complex numbers in polynomial identities and equations.
data.description: (+) Extend polynomial identities to the complex numbers. For example, rewrite x^2 + 4 as (x + 2i)(x – 2i).

data.title: N-CN.9
data.cluster: Use complex numbers in polynomial identities and equations.
data.description: (+) Know the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra; show that it is true for quadratic polynomials.

data.title: N-Q.1
data.cluster: Reason quantitatively and use units to solve problems.
data.description: Use units as a way to understand problems and to guide the solution of multi-step problems; choose and interpret units consistently in formulas; choose and interpret the scale and the origin in graphs and data displays.

data.title: N-Q.2
data.cluster: Reason quantitatively and use units to solve problems.
data.description: Define appropriate quantities for the purpose of descriptive modeling.

data.title: N-Q.3
data.cluster: Reason quantitatively and use units to solve problems.
data.description: Choose a level of accuracy appropriate to limitations on measurement when reporting quantities.

data.title: N-RN.1
data.cluster: Extend the properties of exponents to rational exponents.
data.description: Explain how the definition of the meaning of rational exponents follows from extending the properties of integer exponents to those values, allowing for a notation for radicals in terms of rational exponents. For example, we define 5^1/3 to be the cube root of 5 because we want (5^1/3)^3 = 5^(1/3)3 to hold, so (5^1/3)^3 must equal 5.

data.title: N-RN.2
data.cluster: Extend the properties of exponents to rational exponents.
data.description: Rewrite expressions involving radicals and rational exponents using the properties of exponents.

data.title: N-RN.3
data.cluster: Use properties of rational and irrational numbers.
data.description: Explain why the sum or product of two rational numbers is rational; that the sum of a rational number and an irrational number is irrational; and that the product of a nonzero rational number and an irrational number is irrational.

data.title: N-VM.1
data.cluster: Represent and model with vector quantities.
data.description: (+) Recognize vector quantities as having both magnitude and direction. Represent vector quantities by directed line segments, and use appropriate symbols for vectors and their magnitudes (e.g., v, |v|, ||v||, v).

data.title: N-VM.10
data.cluster: Perform operations on matrices and use matrices in applications.
data.description: (+) Understand that the zero and identity matrices play a role in matrix addition and multiplication similar to the role of 0 and 1 in the real numbers. The determinant of a square matrix is nonzero if and only if the matrix has a multiplicative inverse.

data.title: N-VM.11
data.cluster: Perform operations on matrices and use matrices in applications.
data.description: (+) Multiply a vector (regarded as a matrix with one column) by a matrix of suitable dimensions to produce another vector. Work with matrices as transformations of vectors.

data.title: N-VM.12
data.cluster: Perform operations on matrices and use matrices in applications.
data.description: (+) Work with 2 × 2 matrices as transformations of the plane, and interpret the absolute value of the determinant in terms of area.

data.title: N-VM.2
data.cluster: Represent and model with vector quantities.
data.description: (+) Find the components of a vector by subtracting the coordinates of an initial point from the coordinates of a terminal point.

data.title: N-VM.3
data.cluster: Represent and model with vector quantities.
data.description: (+) Solve problems involving velocity and other quantities that can be represented by vectors.

data.title: N-VM.4a
data.description: Add vectors end-to-end, component-wise, and by the parallelogram rule. Understand that the magnitude of a sum of two vectors is typically not the sum of the magnitudes.

data.title: N-VM.4b
data.description: Given two vectors in magnitude and direction form, determine the magnitude and direction of their sum.

data.title: N-VM.4c
data.description: Understand vector subtraction v – w as v + (–w), where –w is the additive inverse of w, with the same magnitude as w and pointing in the opposite direction. Represent vector subtraction graphically by connecting the tips in the appropriate order, and perform vector subtraction component-wise.

data.title: N-VM.5a
data.description: Represent scalar multiplication graphically by scaling vectors and possibly reversing their direction; perform scalar multiplication component-wise, e.g., as c(vx, vy) = (cvx, cvy).

data.title: N-VM.5b
data.description: Compute the magnitude of a scalar multiple cv using ||cv|| = |c|v. Compute the direction of cv knowing that when |c|v ≠ 0, the direction of cv is either along v (for c > 0) or against v (for c < 0).

data.title: N-VM.6
data.cluster: Perform operations on matrices and use matrices in applications.
data.description: (+) Use matrices to represent and manipulate data, e.g., to represent payoffs or incidence relationships in a network.

data.title: N-VM.7
data.cluster: Perform operations on matrices and use matrices in applications.
data.description: (+) Multiply matrices by scalars to produce new matrices, e.g., as when all of the payoffs in a game are doubled.

data.title: N-VM.8
data.cluster: Perform operations on matrices and use matrices in applications.
data.description: (+) Add, subtract, and multiply matrices of appropriate dimensions.

data.title: N-VM.9
data.cluster: Perform operations on matrices and use matrices in applications.
data.description: (+) Understand that, unlike multiplication of numbers, matrix multiplication for square matrices is not a commutative operation, but still satisfies the associative and distributive properties.

data.title: Describe events as subsets of a sample space
data.domain: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability
data.cluster: Understand independence and conditional probability and use them to interpret data
data.description: Describe events as subsets of a sample space (the set of outcomes) using characteristics (or categories) of the outcomes, or as unions, intersections, or complements of other events (“or,” “and,” “not”).

data.title: Understand independent events
data.domain: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability
data.cluster: Understand independence and conditional probability and use them to interpret data
data.description: Understand that two events A and B are independent if the probability of A and B occurring together is the product of their probabilities, and use this characterization to determine if they are independent.

data.title: Understand conditional probability and independence
data.domain: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability
data.cluster: Understand independence and conditional probability and use them to interpret data
data.description: Understand the conditional probability of A given B as P(A and B)/P(B), and interpret independence of A and B as saying that the conditional probability of A given B is the same as the probability of A, and the conditional probability of B given A is the same as the probability of B.

data.title: Construct and interpret two-way frequency tables
data.domain: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability
data.cluster: Understand independence and conditional probability and use them to interpret data
data.description: Construct and interpret two-way frequency tables of data when two categories are associated with each object being classified. Use the two-way table as a sample space to decide if events are independent and to approximate conditional probabilities. For example, collect data from a random sample of students in your school on their favorite subject among math, science, and English. Estimate the probability that a randomly selected student from your school will favor science given that the student is in tenth grade. Do the same for other subjects and compare the results.

data.title: Recognize conditional probability and independence in everyday situations
data.domain: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability
data.cluster: Understand independence and conditional probability and use them to interpret data
data.description: Recognize and explain the concepts of conditional probability and independence in everyday language and everyday situations. For example, compare the chance of having lung cancer if you are a smoker with the chance of being a smoker if you have lung cancer.

data.title: Find conditional probability as a fraction of outcomes
data.domain: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability
data.cluster: Use the rules of probability to compute probabilities of compound events in a uniform probability model
data.description: Find the conditional probability of A given B as the fraction of B’s outcomes that also belong to A, and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

data.title: Apply the Addition Rule
data.domain: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability
data.cluster: Use the rules of probability to compute probabilities of compound events in a uniform probability model
data.description: Apply the Addition Rule, P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) – P(A and B), and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

data.title: Apply the general Multiplication Rule
data.domain: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability
data.cluster: Use the rules of probability to compute probabilities of compound events in a uniform probability model
data.description: (+) Apply the general Multiplication Rule in a uniform probability model, P(A and B) = P(A)P(B|A) = P(B)P(A|B), and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

data.title: Use permutations and combinations
data.domain: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability
data.cluster: Use the rules of probability to compute probabilities of compound events in a uniform probability model
data.description: (+) Use permutations and combinations to compute probabilities of compound events and solve problems.

data.title: Understand statistics as a process for making inferences
data.cluster: Understand and evaluate random processes underlying statistical experiments
data.description: Understand statistics as a process for making inferences about population parameters based on a random sample from that population.

data.title: Decide if a model is consistent with results
data.cluster: Understand and evaluate random processes underlying statistical experiments
data.description: Decide if a specified model is consistent with results from a given data-generating process, e.g., using simulation. For example, a model says a spinning coin falls heads up with probability 0.5. Would a result of 5 tails in a row cause you to question the model?

data.title: Recognize purposes of surveys, experiments, and observational studies
data.cluster: Make inferences and justify conclusions from sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies
data.description: Recognize the purposes of and differences among sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies; explain how randomization relates to each.

data.title: Use sample survey data to estimate population mean or proportion
data.cluster: Make inferences and justify conclusions from sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies
data.description: Use data from a sample survey to estimate a population mean or proportion; develop a margin of error through the use of simulation models for random sampling.

data.title: Use randomized experiment data to compare treatments
data.cluster: Make inferences and justify conclusions from sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies
data.description: Use data from a randomized experiment to compare two treatments; use simulations to decide if differences between parameters are significant.

data.title: Evaluate reports based on data
data.cluster: Make inferences and justify conclusions from sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies
data.description: Evaluate reports based on data.

data.title: Represent data with plots
data.cluster: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable
data.description: Represent data with plots on the real number line (dot plots, histograms, and box plots).

data.title: Compare center and spread of data distributions
data.cluster: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable
data.description: Use statistics appropriate to the shape of the data distribution to compare center (median, mean) and spread (interquartile range, standard deviation) of two or more different data sets.

data.title: Interpret differences in shape, center, and spread
data.cluster: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable
data.description: Interpret differences in shape, center, and spread in the context of the data sets, accounting for possible effects of extreme data points (outliers).

data.title: Use mean and standard deviation for normal distributions
data.cluster: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable
data.description: Use the mean and standard deviation of a data set to fit it to a normal distribution and to estimate population percentages. Recognize that there are data sets for which such a procedure is not appropriate. Use calculators, spreadsheets, and tables to estimate areas under the normal curve.

data.title: Summarize categorical data in two-way frequency tables
data.cluster: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on two categorical and quantitative variables
data.description: Summarize categorical data for two categories in two-way frequency tables. Interpret relative frequencies in the context of the data (including joint, marginal, and conditional relative frequencies). Recognize possible associations and trends in the data.

data.title: Represent data on two quantitative variables on a scatter plot
data.cluster: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on two categorical and quantitative variables
data.description: Represent data on two quantitative variables on a scatter plot, and describe how the variables are related.

data.title: Fit a function to data
data.cluster: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on two categorical and quantitative variables
data.description: Fit a function to the data; use functions fitted to data to solve problems in the context of the data. Use given functions or choose a function suggested by the context. Emphasize linear, quadratic, and exponential models.

data.title: Assess fit of a function using residuals
data.cluster: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on two categorical and quantitative variables
data.description: Informally assess the fit of a function by plotting and analyzing residuals.

data.title: Fit a linear function for linear associations
data.cluster: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on two categorical and quantitative variables
data.description: Fit a linear function for a scatter plot that suggests a linear association.

data.title: Interpret slope and intercept of a linear model
data.description: Interpret the slope (rate of change) and the intercept (constant term) of a linear model in the context of the data.

data.title: Compute and interpret correlation coefficient
data.description: Compute (using technology) and interpret the correlation coefficient of a linear fit.

data.title: Distinguish between correlation and causation
data.description: Distinguish between correlation and causation.

data.title: Define a random variable
data.cluster: Calculate expected values and use them to solve problems
data.description: (+) Define a random variable for a quantity of interest by assigning a numerical value to each event in a sample space; graph the corresponding probability distribution using the same graphical displays as for data distributions.

data.title: Calculate expected value of a random variable
data.cluster: Calculate expected values and use them to solve problems
data.description: (+) Calculate the expected value of a random variable; interpret it as the mean of the probability distribution.

data.title: Develop a probability distribution (theoretical)
data.cluster: Calculate expected values and use them to solve problems
data.description: (+) Develop a probability distribution for a random variable defined for a sample space in which theoretical probabilities can be calculated; find the expected value. For example, find the theoretical probability distribution for the number of correct answers obtained by guessing on all five questions of a multiple-choice test where each question has four choices, and find the expected grade under various grading schemes.

data.title: Develop a probability distribution (empirical)
data.cluster: Calculate expected values and use them to solve problems
data.description: (+) Develop a probability distribution for a random variable defined for a sample space in which probabilities are assigned empirically; find the expected value. For example, find a current data distribution on the number of TV sets per household in the United States, and calculate the expected number of sets per household. How many TV sets would you expect to find in 100 randomly selected households?

data.title: Weigh possible outcomes of a decision
data.cluster: Use probability to evaluate outcomes of decisions
data.description: (+) Weigh the possible outcomes of a decision by assigning probabilities to payoff values and finding expected values.

data.title: Find expected payoff
data.cluster: Use probability to evaluate outcomes of decisions
data.description: Find the expected payoff for a game of chance. For example, find the expected winnings from a state lottery ticket or a game at a fast-food restaurant.

data.title: Evaluate and compare strategies
data.cluster: Use probability to evaluate outcomes of decisions
data.description: Evaluate and compare strategies on the basis of expected values. For example, compare a high-deductible versus a low-deductible automobile insurance policy using various, but reasonable, chances of having a minor or a major accident.

data.title: Use probabilities to make fair decisions
data.cluster: Use probability to evaluate outcomes of decisions
data.description: (+) Use probabilities to make fair decisions (e.g., drawing by lots, using a random number generator).

data.title: Analyze decisions and strategies
data.cluster: Use probability to evaluate outcomes of decisions
data.description: (+) Analyze decisions and strategies using probability concepts (e.g., product testing, medical testing, pulling a hockey goalie at the end of a game).

data.title: Les droits fondamentaux s’exercent dans le cadre de la loi

data.title: Les droits dits « de troisième génération »

data.description: Approfondir avec les droits dits « de troisième génération », qui résultent du droit de chacun de « vivre dans un environnement équilibré et respectueux de la santé » (art. 1er de la Charte de l’environnement).

data.title: La laïcité garantit la liberté de conscience et l’égalité
data.subject: Enseignement moral et civique
data.domain: Respecter des règles et en comprendre la finalité : l’exemple de la laïcité à l’École
data.description: La laïcité garantit la liberté de conscience et l’égalité de toutes les citoyennes et tous les citoyens, quelles que soient leurs croyances ou opinions ; la neutralité de l’État à l’égard des religions et le libre exercice des cultes (loi de 1905).

data.title: La liberté de conscience : croire, ne pas croire, changer
data.subject: Enseignement moral et civique

data.description: La liberté de conscience est celle de croire, celle de ne pas croire, celle aussi de changer de croyance ou de religion.

data.title: La laïcité, principe juridique et non opinion
data.subject: Enseignement moral et civique
data.domain: Respecter des règles et en comprendre la finalité : l’exemple de la laïcité à l’École
data.description: La laïcité est un principe juridique et non une opinion ; elle diffère par conséquent de l’athéisme ou de l’agnosticisme, qui constituent des options philosophiques personnelles.

data.title: La laïcité à l’école protège la liberté de choix de l’enfant
data.subject: Enseignement moral et civique

data.description: La laïcité à l’école protège la liberté de choix de chaque enfant : elle crée un espace neutre à l’abri des prosélytismes (loi du 15 mars 2004 ; Charte de la laïcité).

data.title: La laïcité impose des règles à la communauté scolaire
data.subject: Enseignement moral et civique

data.description: Dans ce but, la laïcité impose des règles à tous les membres de la communauté scolaire ; elle prépare les élèves à vivre dans une communauté nationale où différentes opinions philosophiques et religieuses peuvent s’exprimer et être discutées dans le cadre de la loi.
